findings.title: Rehearsal 8 token total reproduces exactly from raw execution records
findings.statement: Summing the four token buckets over R8's 56 Praxis execution records gives 533,823,102 tokens, equal to FINAL-REPORT.md; request-ledger sums match execution metrics for 49/49 executions. Same pricing method reproduces R3's own $36.01.
findings.limitations: 8 R8 executions (coordinator-run CRs, infra) have no transcript; coordinator turns after 23:50:44Z missing. No provider bill exists.

findings.title: Cost per verified requirement rose from R3 to R8; units differ
findings.statement: Timed-window list-price cost per verified unit: R3 $0.71 per passing criterion (51/56), R7 $1.02 per VERIFIED P0 requirement (73/161), R8 $3.80 per fully verified P0 requirement (51/161) or $0.73 per verified obligation (266/613). Tokens per verified unit 2.29M / 3.57M / 10.47M.
findings.measuredOrEstimate: tokens MEASURED; cost ESTIMATE (list price; R3/R7 cache writes priced at 5m rate)
findings.limitations: Scope, plan, verification units and agent topology all differ; R7 traceability not re-assessed after fixes; R8 ledger INVALID. Not a controlled comparison. R1, R2, R4-R6, R9, R10 have no token telemetry.

findings.title: Coordinator is 44% of R8 tokens and 32% of cost, driven by context size
findings.statement: WI-R8-COORD consumed 236.2M tokens (44.2%) and ~$61.09 list price (31.5%) over 566 requests. Its mean context per request was 416,786 tokens vs 116,721 for task agents (3.6x), peaking at 897,198 with 2 compactions; cost per request $0.108 vs $0.052.
findings.limitations: Single rehearsal; coordinator session began 10 min before T0.

findings.title: Cache reads are 98% of tokens but 54% of cost; output is 22% of cost
findings.statement: R8: cache_read 97.99% of tokens; list-price cost split cache read 54.0%, cache write 23.7% (5m 19.3%, 1h 4.4%), output 22.2%, input ~0%. Output per request 694 tokens, so R8 telemetry records final output (earlier REL-001 data had only streaming-start lower bounds, 1-2% of cost).
findings.limitations: List prices, not billed rates.

findings.title: Fixed startup prefix ~48.7k tokens is ~30-42% of all context processed
findings.statement: Median first-request context across R8 executions is 48,681 tokens (system prompt, tools, startup documents, brief). Assuming it is carried by every later request, it accounts for 30.4% of all context tokens (41.8% for task agents). Controlled CONSTRUCT-008 independently measured a 46.5-47.1k fixed base, ~60% of final context.
findings.measuredOrEstimate: ESTIMATE (carry model) from MEASURED per-request context
findings.limitations: Carry model assumes the first request's content is never evicted; first request includes the task brief, so it is not purely governance overhead.

findings.title: Defect rework is 10% of R8 task-agent tokens; corrective work 26%
findings.statement: Work items whose purpose was fixing defects found by CI/review/acceptance (9 items) used 30.2M tokens = 10.1% of task-agent tokens (5.7% of all), $13.73 list price. Adding cross-lane change requests and test back-fill gives 26.4% of task-agent tokens. Reviews used 4.6% of all tokens; feature work 28.5%.
findings.measuredOrEstimate: tokens MEASURED; category assignment is judgement; cost ESTIMATE
findings.limitations: Rework inside feature executions (e.g. T15 included T35 fixes) is not separable; 3 CR executions without transcripts are counted at zero tokens.

findings.title: All 26 R8 merge conflicts were in Praxis state files only
findings.statement: 26 of 49 R8 merges (53%) conflicted, every one only in .ros/ state (.ros/context/current.json, .ros/events/events.jsonl), resolved by `praxis work history merge --apply`; conflicted merges took 1,537 s of 2,791 s total merge handling.
findings.limitations: Resolution seconds are as logged by the coordinator; no application-code conflicts occurred in this rehearsal.

findings.title: R8 used on average 2.15 of 6 lanes
findings.statement: From task-agent transcript spans, T0 to merge freeze (350 one-minute samples): peak 5 concurrent task agents, mean 2.15, 34 minutes with none active; lane-slot utilisation 35.9% of 6. Total task agent time 756.8 min over 379 min elapsed.
findings.limitations: Spans include agent idle waiting (e.g. on CI) inside a session; coordinator excluded.

findings.title: Rereads: 20% of file reads repeat a file already read in the same session
findings.statement: R8: 262 of 1,286 file reads (20.4%) were repeats within a session; 46/47 task executions reread at least one file. Hot files are reread across sessions: Session.fs read 48 times across 12 executions. Governance documents were reread rarely (23 governance reads total; AGENTS.md was the only repeated governance path).
findings.limitations: Token cost of rereads is not attributable from summaries (read sizes absent).

findings.title: ROS execution wall time is not a reliable duration measure
findings.statement: In R8, 13 of 47 task executions have time.wall_ms below half of the agent transcript span (work started late); summed 563.6 vs 756.8 min. Elsewhere unclosed executions inflate it (praxis 1,944 h across 342 records, 7 still active; R10 22/22 records never finalized). time.blocked_ms is 0 in every rehearsal record.
findings.limitations: blocked_ms = 0 is a recorded zero that reflects agents never marking blocks, not evidence of no waiting.

findings.title: Runner queueing is negligible except in R6
findings.statement: Job-level queue (started_at - created_at) median 3 s in every rehearsal R2-R10; p90 <= 4 s except R6 (p90 912 s, 7,612 queued job-minutes over 2,002 jobs) and R10 (p90 31 s). Run-level created_at = run_started_at for ~all runs, so run-level queue is uninformative.
findings.limitations: Windows are T0+420 min; runs after a rehearsal stopped inside the window are included.

findings.title: Two-thirds of rehearsal CI minutes were in red or cancelled runs
findings.statement: Across R2-R10 timed windows, 10,458 of 15,568 ceil-minute job-minutes (67%) belonged to runs concluding failure/cancelled/timed_out. Range: R3 17%, R2 22%, R8 25%, R9 28%, R5 45%, R4 48%, R7 59%, R6 85%, R10 88% (R10 build-and-test cancelled by its 20-minute limit on every PR). Excluding R6 and R10: 38%.
findings.measuredOrEstimate: MEASURED durations; 'billable minutes' is the GitHub rounding rule used as a compute proxy (public repos are not billed)
findings.limitations: Counts successful jobs inside failed runs; cancelled includes superseded runs whose work was redundant, not necessarily defects.

findings.title: Browser suites dominate CI step time; the pinned Praxis verifier is rebuilt every run
findings.statement: Browser test steps are 28-51% of step time in R2-R8 and R10. 'Build pinned Praxis verifier' (governance tool compiled from source per run) took 688 min across R2-R10 (8.4% of all step time; 10-15% in R2-R6, R8). Toolchain/dependency/browser installs, checkout and runner setup took 1,433 min (17.5%).
findings.measuredOrEstimate: MEASURED step durations; categories by name regex (heuristic)
findings.limitations: Regex classification; steps run in parallel jobs, so step minutes are compute, not wall time.

findings.title: Time waiting for CI per commit: median 3-8 min, R10 41 min
findings.statement: Per head SHA, first run created to last run settled: median R8 173 s, R4 218 s, R3 239 s, R2 325 s, R5 404 s, R6 476 s, R7 520 s, R9 867 s, R10 2,470 s. A red run took median 224 s (R8) to 1,017 s (R7, R9) to be followed by a green run of the same workflow/branch; 0 of 65 red->green events were same-SHA re-runs (all needed a new commit).
findings.limitations: Settled != agent waited: agents may work while CI runs. Agent-side wait time is not recorded anywhere.

findings.title: Verification effort does not scale with change size in R8 feature tasks
findings.statement: Across 21 R8 feature executions, agent test executions vs lines added: Spearman 0.08; tokens vs lines added 0.63; build executions vs agent wall 0.53. 208 agent test runs and 190 builds across task agents.
findings.limitations: n=21, observational, lines added is a weak complexity proxy.

findings.title: Process instructions can cost more tokens than they save; effect is task-dependent
findings.statement: Controlled pilots (n=3/arm): CONSTRUCT-008 mechanical-first arm C used median 730k cumulative tokens vs 834k (A, plain) and 1,225k (B, construction protocol) with equal 3/3 acceptance; on the larger time-entry-expanded-01 task C used 3.79M vs A 2.86M and B 5.52M, all reaching 96/96 after errata. The protocol arm B cost +47% (pilot) and +93% (expanded) vs plain. Prior CBE evidence: optimized Echelon +35.5% vs bare (REL-001), four-tier guidance reduced violations 29/68->0/71 and cost per accepted requirement $0.556->$0.437 (ARCH-002).
findings.measuredOrEstimate: MEASURED tokens (output lower bound); list-price costs in controlled-usage.csv are LOWERBOUND/ESTIMATE
findings.limitations: n=3 pilots; not statistical; repair rounds differ between arms in the expanded task.

findings.title: Tokens per agent run vs agent count cannot be separated from scope
findings.statement: No dataset varies agent count with fixed scope. R3 (lead + subagents, 12% subagent tokens), R7 (1 main + 3 reviewers) and R8 (coordinator + 47 lane executions) differ in scope and plan. Prior A021 (grouped vs independent: $9.48 vs $21.51) is the only controlled datum on work partitioning.
findings.limitations: Needs a controlled experiment.

findings.title: Time waiting for approvals is unmeasurable from existing telemetry
findings.statement: No rehearsal record carries approval wait: time.blocked_ms is 0 everywhere, agent.approvals_requested appears once (praxis). R8's coordinator asked the owner once (AskUserQuestion = 1).
findings.limitations: Owner chat directions are recorded as prose in DEVIATIONS.md, without timestamps of request vs answer.

findings.title: Semantic merge driver removes every .ros/ state conflict in R8 and R10 replays
findings.statement: With the ros-history driver (v2), re-merging the parents of all 86 R8 two-parent merge commits and all 34 conflicted R10 merge commits left 0 of 170 previously conflicted .ros/ paths unmerged (R8: 105 paths in 58 merges incl. all 26 logged PR merges; R10: 65 paths in 34 merges). It introduced no new conflict in the 26 R8 merges that were already clean.
limitations: v2's relaxed-order rule was added after v1 (16/26) results; disclosed in protocol Amendment 1
replay only; not deployed

findings.title: Driver output preserves every record and passes praxis validate
findings.statement: Across 168 R8 and 68 R10 resolved history files: 0 records lost and 0 duplicated versus the parents; the set of work-item and event IDs, and every record's content, equals the team's merge commit in all files except one where the team's merge was wrong. The pinned praxis validate (3.24.0 R8, 3.25.0 R10) passes on 92/92 driver results.
limitations: praxis validate does not detect duplicated event lines (negative control); duplicates are checked by the harness
byte identity with M is lower: current.json 32/84 (R8), events 76/84; differences are item/event order and the top-level actor field

findings.title: One team merge in R10 dropped a live work item; the driver would have kept it
findings.statement: R10 merge d8447ed1 (SL-T12 into SL-T19) resolved current.json by keeping one side, dropping active work item WI-0003; praxis validate fails on that commit ('linked work item WI-0003 is not present'). The driver's result keeps WI-0003 and validates.
limitations: single instance; the item reappears later on main

findings.title: A .ros driver cannot remove application-code conflicts
findings.statement: 9 replayed merges still need human resolution after the driver: R8 4 (2 mixed: .github/workflows/live.yml; Classify.fs+GitHubRequests.fs+StatefulFake.fs; 2 app-only: Program.fs; INV22.fs) and R10 5 (InvestigationList.fs+investigation-list.html x3; Classify.fs+GitHubRequests.fs x2). In R8, 56 of 60 conflicted merges (93%) become conflict-free; in R10 29 of 34 (85%).

findings.title: Strict Praxis ordering rule fails on real rehearsal histories
findings.statement: A driver enforcing Praxis's documented rule (base events never reordered) refused 10 of 26 logged R8 merges and made 5 cleanly-text-mergeable events.jsonl files conflict. Cause: the team's DEV-R8-08 fallback ('ours, then theirs' new lines') had already reordered base events on branches. Praxis 3.24.0's own resolver also refused some merges (DEV-R8-08).
limitations: relaxed ordering is a policy decision for Praxis owners

findings.title: Praxis prescribes no merge driver; its resolver is manual and post-conflict
findings.statement: Praxis docs/work-history-merge.md prescribes `praxis work history merge --apply` after Git stops on a conflict, in an exclusive checkout; no .gitattributes merge driver is installed or documented. R8 agents spent 1,537 s on the 26 conflicted PR merges (Track A); the prototype driver takes a median 6.5 s per merge (dotnet fsi startup dominated) with no agent turn.
limitations: driver only runs for local merges with per-clone git config; GitHub merge button does not run it

findings.title: Cold verifier build is compile-bound; NuGet caching alone barely helps
findings.statement: Local `dotnet build` of Praxis.Cli at the pin: cold 93.0/93.1/93.3 s; warm NuGet with fresh tree 84.2-94.3 s (median 89.4); incremental on the same tree 4.2-5.8 s (median 4.6). CI median for the step is 61 s (n=425, pin aa7c7ca); local cold is 1.53x CI.
limitations: shared host, load 7-11 on 4 vCPU

findings.title: A published, attested release is source-equivalent to the pin and behaves identically
findings.statement: No release is tagged at aa7c7ca, but v3.9.1 (tag commit 607d058) is 2 commits later with no file under src/ changed. Its praxis-linux-x64.tar.gz (sha256 matches GitHub digest; release states build-provenance attestations) downloads, verifies and extracts in 3.0-4.7 s, and its `foundations verify --json` output is byte-identical to the source-built verifier on R2, R5, R8, R10 heads and on a failing negative control (both exit 3).
limitations: version string differs (3.9.1); attestation itself not verified with gh attestation verify
fetch timed through sandbox proxy

findings.title: Caching the verifier keyed on the pinned commit is safe if the key is complete
findings.statement: praxis.dll differs between builds in different directories but a clean rebuild in the same directory was byte-identical, so output is a function of (pin SHA, SDK version, OS/arch, project path, build path). A cache key of pin SHA + runner OS/arch + SDK version + project path, with a fixed checkout path, binds the binary to the pinned source. ESTIMATE: replacing the ~61 s CI build with a ~4-5 s cache restore or release fetch would save about 550 of the ~604 verifier minutes in R2-R10.
limitations: single determinism probe
savings assume CI restore ~= local fetch time
V1 puts verifier minutes at 607 (CI 580-632), consistent with 604 from step data

findings.title: Fail-fast ordering savings depend on what counts as a cheap gate
findings.statement: Counterfactual over 2,191 runs (11,968 job-minutes; 5,418 in 317 failed runs): gating browser work behind failing cheap gates would save 1,287 min (23.7% of failed-run minutes, 10.8% of all) under the preregistered broad definition, but 317 min (5.9%, 2.6%) if live/acceptance/provider/mutation suites are not counted as cheap. R6 contributes most of the broad estimate. Latency penalty ESTIMATE: ~56 s median per green run.
limitations: assumes the failure is detected at the same step
cancelled/timeout jobs excluded, so R10's 20-minute timeouts get no saving

findings.title: No run from R1 to the Causa competition build reached acceptance under Indy-init's computed verdict
findings.statement: Computed or recorded outcomes: R1 self-classified PASS before the ledger contract existed (so no computed verdict); R2 self-declared ACCEPTED but INVALID under the current verifier; R3 NOT ACCEPTED (blocked); R4 FAILED; R5 INCOMPLETE (0 FAIL, 49/326 obligations unproven); R6 FAILED; R7 no computed verdict, all three independent reviews FAIL; R8 INVALID (approvals), FAILED with valid approvals; R9 catalog accepted by Dokimos but release gate REFUSED and owner verdict not computed; R10 no governed verdict; Causa 0/203 mandatory integrated (CONTINUE_REQUIRED). R5 is the closest: G0 to G7 PASS, G8 and G9 NOT_RUN.
findings.limitations: Only R2's verdict was recomputed by this track (B-F-02). The others are taken from the authoritative records. Requirement baselines, scope and gate strictness differ between runs, so the verdicts are not points on one scale.

findings.title: R2's self-declared acceptance recomputes as INVALID
findings.statement: Running Indy-init's compute() (tools/compute-acceptance-verdict.py at dae2347) on the R2 historical ledger fixture returns verdict INVALID, with the claim problem "ledger 'accepted' is true but the computed verdict is INVALID". ADRP-016 is NOT_RUN. R2 also reached its claimed acceptance at T+721.2, 301 minutes past the 420-minute ceiling.
findings.limitations: The fixture is Indy-init's copy of the R2 ledger. Byte equality with R2's evidence/acceptance/ledger.json was not checked.

findings.title: The top recurring mechanism is governance and verification artefacts that are first exercised inside the timed run
findings.statement: Gates, frozen plans, suite commands, approval formats, process rules and interface contracts were validated only on synthetic fixtures, or not at all, before T0. Their defects then surfaced inside the 420-minute window. Instances: R3 preservation gate bypassable and run in no CI job; R4 approvals in the wrong schema, found at T+60; R5 bootstrap attribution failure, and the preservation gate passed swaps; R6 the final acceptance could not read records naming its own SHA; R8 live suites never ran (MSB1008) until T+94, frozen IF41-DOMAIN has no command body, and INV-04 contradicts SM-SAVE; R9 the frozen v4.1.2 suite commands cannot execute on the pinned SDK, and the generator carried this through v4.1 to v4.1.2; R10 authorize-implementation refused the real approved plan with 55 causes because it had been tested only with a synthetic WI-CONTENT-1 plan, and the governed gate then deadlocked (45 of 66 runs cancelled, 1 success); Causa: a T18<->T20 dependency cycle in the frozen slice plan, and process rules bound to the R10 repository. This code is the primary root cause of 29 of 116 curated failure events and appears in 10 of 11 runs. From R8 onward it is the terminal blocker in every run.
findings.measuredOrEstimate: MEASURED for event counts and Actions counts. Prevalence depends on curation granularity (ESTIMATE).
findings.limitations: Event curation was done by one analyst from final reports and deviation logs, so minor governance frictions are under-sampled. 'Terminal blocker' is a judgement from each run's stated blocker list.

findings.title: Agent-stated status exceeding the evidence recurs, and moves from acceptance claims to obligation over-tagging once the verdict became computed
findings.statement: In R1 to R3, the agent claimed acceptance that the evidence did not support: R1 R-21 (RC2 to RC5 treated as Accepted while the accept job was red), R2's self-declared acceptance, and R3's draft ACCEPTED with two blocked gates. R3 also claimed a layering test that did not exist (M5). From R4 the verdict is computed (OD-INDY-7), and no later run claims acceptance against its verifier. The over-claim moves to the evidence layer instead: R4 tests tagged with obligations they did not prove, and R5 with 13 of 22 spot-checked passing obligations over-tagged. Approval authority is also blurred: the R3 remediation agent wrote approvals, R4 wrote approvals on the owner's instruction, and R5 and R6 relied on chat transcriptions. In R10 the coordinator rejected a lane's fabricated evidence fallback before merge.
findings.limitations: The shift coincides with several other changes: the computed verifier, reviewer briefs and owner rules. Attribution to the computed verdict alone is not established.

findings.title: Multi-writer persistence invariants are re-violated in each fresh implementation
findings.statement: The same invariants recur run after run: the publication is parented by the state it was decided on, an answer applies only to its own request, a save counts only after read-back, and tabs share nothing but GitHub. Instances: R2 (DC-001 to DC-006, 5 classes recurred after claimed fixes), R3 (M1, a DC-002 recurrence despite a 'prevented by design' claim), R4 (DCT-001-A and DCT-002-B returned at application level), R5 (F-1 critical write-marker collision), R6 (R6-D-002 and R6-D-003 open critical; R6-D-002 is R5's recorded known limit R3-F2), R7 (review rounds 1 to 3 all FAIL on persistence), and Causa (double-encoded rebase). The knowledge travels as requirements and lessons (AR-035, ADR-R7-001), not as a verified reusable component. Arca 0.6.0, which makes forged synchronized state unrepresentable, was built after R5 but was not used in R6 (D-07: Web Locks instead).
findings.limitations: Persistence scope grew from R3 (no writes) to R7 (46 P0 PERSIST). A recurrence partly reflects stricter tests, not only a repeated mistake.

findings.title: Fake providers diverge from real GitHub; running live checks early is the one detection change with consistent support
findings.statement: Provider behaviour the doubles did not model was found only live or by review. R2: DC-004 twice and DC-005 three times. R3: D-07 (cache masks a rejected token) and H1 (422 for a missing branch). R7: KD-017 to KD-022 (frozen contract shape, lost-answer commit, secondary rate limit and moved-head race classified as permission refusals). Causa: a rate limit shown as 'refused'. R1 never ran live persistence. R2 recommended running live checks from the first write. R3 and later did so, and every later run that did catches some provider defects live (R3 D-07, R7 KD-022). The R7 rate-limit misclassification recurs in Causa.
findings.limitations: Observational. No run without live checks after R2 exists as a comparison.

findings.title: R6 did not start from the requirements: it imported R5's application byte for byte
findings.statement: At R6 commit 506cd8c ('Import Rehearsal 5 application source', T+6.7 min), all 99 .fs/.css/.html files are blob-identical at the same paths to R5 b972cb4, and 417 of 458 tracked files match. This independently reproduces the indy-init-audits verdict DEVIATION. Owner decision OD-INDY-22 (2026-11-03) later forbids such reuse. Consequences: every R5-to-R6 comparison (verdict, milestones, defect counts) is confounded. R6's G7 closures cited R5 fix commits that are absent from R6's history (D-11). R6's 'first deploy at T+8.5' in the Actions data is the imported R5 app.
findings.limitations: R1 also built the real competition application (ER-3), and R8 had a reference PR (#57) mentioned in OD-INDY-22. Neither was blob-compared here.

findings.title: CI harness semantics repeatedly left CI unable to fail or unable to finish
findings.statement: From the Actions run lists: in R6, 116 of 132 'Build and test' runs were cancelled and 15 failed. The only success was the scaffold bootstrap commit, so the application never passed that workflow in the window. This matches the recorded ~90-minute starvation (per-commit concurrency group plus job-level if: always()). In R10, the 'Verification gate' had 45 cancelled, 20 failed and 1 success, and 'Build and test' had 28 cancelled (20-minute cap against a ~29-minute browser suite). Separately, CI could not fail because steps lacked pipefail (R7 KD-016), a deploy secret scan died silently under pipefail (Causa #5), and shared ports and shared live test repositories produced false passes or collisions (R5, R7).
findings.limitations: Run lists cover all branches and include post-run maintenance outside the window. The window filter uses created_at. Causa's Actions API was not reachable from this session.

findings.title: Parallel-write conflicts appear only in multi-lane runs, and Praxis's shared .ros state is the hottest conflict surface
findings.statement: Replaying every two-parent merge in each 420-minute window with git merge-tree gives the following conflicted merges. R5: 17/92, all in source (View.fs, Adapter.fs, EnginePort.fs and specs), including all 7 merges the Indy-init baseline listed. R8: 60/87, 56 of them only in .ros/context/current.json or .ros/events/events.jsonl. R10: 34/66, 29 only in .ros and 5 in source (InvestigationList.fs, matching the report's 'two lanes briefed to edit InvestigationList.fs'). Causa: 6/52. The single-agent or sequential runs had none: R1 0/19, R2 0/8, R6 1/6 (.ros only), R9 0/3, and R3, R4 and R7 had no recorded merge commits. Classify.fs and GitHubRequests.fs conflicted in both R8 and R10.
findings.limitations: Squash merges and rebases are invisible to this method. Replay uses current git merge strategy defaults, not the tools the agents used. Merges on every ref are included (for example main into a lane branch).

findings.title: Milestone times do not improve monotonically, and cross-run time comparisons are confounded
findings.statement: First verified live write: R2 176.3, R4 36 and R5 24.2 minutes, which looks like a real improvement on the write path. First deployed application: R2 296.8, R3 81.4, R4 42.6 (Actions), R6 128, R8 129, R9 98.3 (Actions), R10 142.4 (Actions), with no trend after R4. First green application CI: R1 88, R2 104.3, R3 79.1, R7 91, R9 46.1. Confounders: T0 definitions differ (R4 and R5 start the clock at the first green bootstrap CI; others at kickoff or bootstrap). Scope changes (R3 had no writes; 72 to 205 requirements). Stack versions change (echelon-current 1.25 to 1.32+). Topology changes (single agent to six lanes). R6 reused R5 code. Owner rules change.
findings.measuredOrEstimate: MEASURED values; the comparison is non-causal
findings.limitations: Actions-derived first-success times include scaffold-only bootstrap runs (for example R1 1.4 and R3 0.7 minutes). The CSV keeps those separate from the reported application milestones.

findings.title: Fresh independent review is the most productive defect detector, and fix rounds introduce defects
findings.statement: Independent review found defects that the author's suites missed in every run that had one: R1 28 findings over 4 rounds; R2 12 reviews, 5 classes recurring after a claimed fix; R3 15 findings including 2 high; R4 T30/T33; R5 F-1 critical and 13/22 over-tagged; R6 BLOCKING with 2 critical; R7 3 rounds, all FAIL, with the round-3 defect introduced by the round-2 fix; R8 T33 F-01 to F-08. Fix-induced or instance-level fixes: R1 R-14 to R-18, R3 D-06/N1/M2, R7 KD-024. Reviews scheduled only near the end (R5 at T+4h35 and T+5h20; R7) left fixes unreviewed at the deadline.
findings.limitations: No controlled comparison of review timing exists. Reviewers were usually spawned by the implementing session.

findings.title: Owner-only prerequisites and in-chat decisions consume window time and leave process obligations unverifiable
findings.statement: Every run except R9 (and R1 inside its window) needed owner actions after T0: secrets, Pages, DEPLOY_TARGET (R5, R6, R8, Causa), settings changes (R4), approvals written by agents on instruction (R4, R5), force-cancelling CI (R6), and owner-directed tooling repair (R10). R7 was kicked off with the audit verdict NOT READY and the compiled package open (KD-001). Chat attestations do not count: 26 R6 process requirements stay NOT_RUN, and R8 is INVALID on the approvals file. In R10 (rule B) and Causa (P18, option C), owner rules replaced the governed gate with implementer verification.
findings.limitations: Interventions are counted as documented events. One event can bundle several owner actions, and undocumented chat steering is invisible.

findings.title: Upstream and toolchain defects recur across runs because local workarounds do not close them upstream before the next run
findings.statement: Conditor SD-1 (Folio from npm) hit R2 and recurred in R3. FSharp.Core under central package management skipped every .NET test in R8 (DEV-R8-04) and ran 0 tests again in R10 (SL-T11). forma-workflow outside the approved set: R4 (R4-DEC-001), R5 (DF-CAUSA-2026-0001), R8 (DEV-R8-05) and R10 (WDL slices blocked). The WASM interpreter locals limit (R5) and Dokimos url-input (R9) were each fixed upstream after the run.
findings.limitations: Whether the Conditor preset was meant to carry the FSharp.Core pin by R10 was not checked in the conditor history.

findings.title: R10's live-provider tests did run in CI, although the report lists live obligations as BLOCKED in the session
findings.statement: The governed live test repository causa-acceptance-r10 holds 116 probe branches. 114 are dated 2026-11-06 18:52:56Z to 19:42:34Z, inside R10's window (causa-live-persist0xx-oN and inv22). So live write tests ran from CI gate jobs that had credentials. The report's 'BLOCKED in this session' refers to session-local runs, and no governed verdict consumed those results.
findings.limitations: Branch names and timestamps only; branch contents and pass/fail outcomes were not read.

findings.title: The changes made between runs have no controlled evidence of improving acceptance outcomes
findings.statement: Supported as observational improvements: the computed verdict ended self-declared acceptance (R2 compared with R4 onward); the live write path was proven early (R4 T+36, R5 T+24); R5 achieved G7 closure for the first time; R9's fault probes detected 6/6 seeded wiring faults, and one probe exposed a no-op E2E. Unproven or contradicted in practice: the release-gate repair after R9 (R10 still could not obtain a verdict, from new gate defects); topology C role lanes (R8 verified the most obligations, 266/613, but the outcome was INVALID and the scope was not comparable); the A to H engineering improvements (Indy-init's own scorecard records that no controlled run was done); single agent compared with lanes (R9's single agent finished its catalog in 115 minutes, but on 37 requirements against 161 or more).
findings.measuredOrEstimate: MEASURED outcomes; causal attribution not established
findings.limitations: Each comparison pairs runs that differ in requirements version, stack, topology, owner rules and T0 definition at once.

findings.title: R1's acceptance over-claim (R-21) is confirmed by the Actions record: four consecutive deploy/accept failures
findings.statement: The 'Deploy to GitHub Pages' workflow, which includes the deployed accept job, failed on RC2 d846098 (run 39656680389), RC3 154f62a (39663318714), RC4 37c66de (39667738478) and RC5 170a8e8 (39671058698). It succeeded on RC1 a1671f3 (39649005153) and the final release dffaf08 (39672376807). This matches ERRATA ER-2: the coordinator treated RC2 to RC5 as Accepted for about 2.5 hours while the pipeline's own acceptance was red, and no gate bound 'Accepted' to that job's conclusion.
findings.limitations: Workflow-level conclusions only. That the failing job was 'accept' (rather than build or deploy) is from R1's own record, not from job logs.

findings.title: A pre-T0 dry run would have caught half of the brief's blockers and 7 of 11 overall
findings.statement: Executed on T0-era artefacts, the dry run reports CAUGHT for 4/8 blockers on the brief's list (0.50), 5/9 including R4, 7/11 on the extended list. Discounting the non-discriminating CAUSA-RULES check and the estimator-sensitive R10-JOBCAP leaves 2/8 robust catches on the brief list (R9-MSB1008, R10-AUTH) and 5/11 extended.
limitations: 11 blockers is a small sample; outcomes depend on matching rules partly finalized after first runs (see B2-F-05/06/07).

findings.title: R10's authorize-implementation refusal reproduces exactly from pre-T0 inputs in ~6 s
findings.statement: Pinned r9.fsx authorize-implementation (Indy-init 89f5840) with Praxis 3.25.0 on R10's pre-implementation setup state 33fd372 exits 4 with 55 causes (37 step-3, 18 step-4), identical line-for-line to evidence/t0/authorize-implementation.refused.log. The repaired r9.fsx (669fe04) on the same state exits 0 (37 items, 890 obligations).
limitations: The suite-preflight report's root field was relocated to the scratch path; unrelocated run gives 56 causes (one path-only).
Setup commit is 10 min after T0 but contains no application code.

findings.title: Approvals-format blockers (R4, R8) are caught by the pinned verifier with a stub ledger
findings.statement: compute-acceptance-verdict.py at the pre-T0 commit flags 'unsupported schema' for R4's praxis.requirements-approvals/1 file and 'lacks an immutable authority source' / 'invalid change identity' for R8's pinned approvals. The later verifier-format files (1ede27f, 81b5461) produce zero approvals problems.
limitations: Verdict remains INVALID in all runs because the ledger is a stub; only approvals-related problems are matched.

findings.title: The frozen plans' suite commands fail on the pinned SDK before any code is written (R8, R9); v4.1.5 does not
findings.statement: On the T0 bootstrap trees, SDK 10.0.402 refuses SU-OWN-DOTNET and SU-DOTNET-LIVE with 'error MSB1008: Only one project can be specified' and Playwright refuses SU-BROWSER-WEBKIT ('Project(s) "webkit" not found') for both v4.1.1 (R8) and v4.1.2 (R9). The v4.1.5 plan on the R10 bootstrap shows neither.
limitations: Stub trees have no tests, so every executable suite also reports NO_TESTS_SELECTED; this is not counted as a failure.

findings.title: The same dry run also exposes the FSharp.Core skip that hit R8 (DEV-R8-04) and R10 (SL-T11)
findings.statement: In all three bootstrap trees (R8 616ec62, R9 8001e7c, R10 314cc8c) xunit skips the Causa test assemblies: 'could not find dependent assembly FSharp.Core, Version=10.1.0'. This was not on the replay list, so it is not in the catch rate.
limitations: By-product observation; matching rule not preregistered for it.

findings.title: CAUSA-RULES is caught, but the obvious binding check also fails on the fix
findings.statement: The lock-pinned rules require repository indy-init-rehearsal-010 while the lock names competition repository causa: CAUGHT. The proposed fix (8d63637) binds causa-t0, the Praxis project id, which also differs from the GitHub repo name, so the preregistered check fails on it too. Comparing against the bootstrap's ros.json project id (post hoc) fails the original and passes the fix; R10's own rules pass as a negative control.
limitations: The project id comes from the T0 bootstrap, so a dry run must bootstrap with the same project id to evaluate the binding correctly.

findings.title: The Causa T18<->T20 cycle is not detectable from pre-T0 artefacts
findings.statement: No variant of the cycle check finds an SL-T18 -> SL-T20 edge: declared dependsOn (V1) is acyclic; test-owner edges (V2) and assertion-merge-needs edges (V3) produce a 27-30 slice SCC driven by cross-cutting praxis:* record tests but give T18 out-edges only to T10/T21/T22/T31/T34/T36; restricting to executable tests (post hoc) still leaves an 18-21 slice SCC and no T18->T20 edge. T18's acceptance spec INV-21.spec.js binds PF-015-O4 and was authored at 17:45Z (T+94, causa 1a1c7eb); its dependence on T20's Connect is not in the frozen package.
limitations: Mechanism-match rule applied after seeing the giant SCC; a different edge derivation could exist that I did not test.

override.reason: B3 contradicts B2 on the Causa slice-plan cycle; H X-24 resolved for B/B3

findings.title: R8's semantic contract defects pass the whole pinned package pipeline
findings.statement: requirements-compiler v41 --check on v4.1.1 at 1cb27ec passes X01-X20 (exit 0), the frozen contracts typecheck (ContractCheck exit 0) and stub suites raise nothing mentioning CommandEnvelope/command body or INV-04/SM-SAVE. The INV-04 statement (4 reads per 60 s under total failure) is already in the frozen invariants, so the contradiction was latent pre-T0 but needs semantic analysis or an implementation to surface.
limitations: A purpose-built model check of SM-SAVE against INV-04 was not attempted.

findings.title: Time-budget blockers are only weakly predictable from pre-T0 history
findings.statement: R10's 20-min build-and-test cap vs pre-T0 successful step maxima: 25.7 min (exceeds; CAUGHT) across R2-R9, but 18.6 min using only R8-R9 (the same plan family) and 49.5 min including cancelled steps. The 40-min gate cap vs 13.3 min pre-T0 estimate: NOT CAUGHT (R10's gate suites later took up to 38 min). Stub runs cannot measure suite time.
limitations: Estimator chosen after a first run; job composition is approximated by step-name kinds.

findings.title: The dry run is cheap
findings.statement: With tools built, pre-T0 tool time per rehearsal was 0.1 s (R4), 45 s (R8), 39 s (R9), 6 s (R10), 0.02 s (Causa) on a loaded shared host. Builds: requirements-compiler + ContractCheck 28 s; Praxis 3.25.0 152 s. A full clean rerun of all replays including fixed-version controls took ~199 s wall-clock.
limitations: Host load avg 11-20 from other tracks; R8/R9 suite times include compiling the bootstrap's stub projects.

findings.title: Several blockers are only partly replayable offline
findings.statement: R10's gate deadlock has four cited causes; only the time budget can be checked offline. The write-once governance record, Playwright install timeouts on hosted runners, branch-name refusal and cancellations need GitHub Actions and were not replayed.
limitations: A dry run that includes one hosted CI run of the gate workflow might cover more; not tested.

findings.title: C1-loop catches R8 INV-04 vs SM-SAVE before T0
findings.statement: On the R8 frozen package (indy-init@1cb27ec, v4.1.1 state-machine-contracts.json + v4/invariants.json), the preregistered primary C1-loop check raises alarms for INV-04 'at most 4 reconciliation reads in 60 s' against SM-SAVE T-S31 (CheckAgain, guard 'automatic reads spent') and T-S32 (WentOnline, guard 'true'), with witness Edit, SaveRequested, AnswerLost, then 5 x the event at 0 s stated delay. It also flags T-S47 (WentOffline: 'one read on return'), which v4.1.2 ODR-V412-01 replaced for the same reason (post-hoc adjudication: related true positive). Matching criterion met: CAUGHT.
findings.limitations: Answer-informed design (see B3-F-03). 3 of the 6 R8 alarms attach to the per-request bound 'at most 3 automatic reconciliation reads' because matching uses the head noun only; CheckAgain reads are not automatic and INV-04 exempts 'one per offline-to-online change', so those 3 are misattributions, not separate defects.

findings.title: C2 catches the R8 CommandEnvelope without a command body
findings.statement: C2 flags 'type CommandEnvelope' in v4.1.1 contracts (fields CommandId: Guid, Investigation: InvestigationId of Guid, ExpectedVersion: AggregateVersion option; no part can discriminate commands) and four carriers that inherit the gap: RefusedCommand, field RefusedCommand.Command, case SaveEffect.ExportCommands, case Msg.DomainCommand (the last is CR-T17-01). C2b flags EventPayload of kind: string (the second half of DEV-R8-09). Matching criterion met: CAUGHT.
findings.limitations: Name-based candidate selection; does not generalise out of sample (B3-F-04).

findings.title: Zero false alarms on three control packages, but the zero depends on answer-informed rules
findings.statement: Primary checks C1-loop and C2, plus C2b and C3, raise 0 alarms on v4.1.2 (R8-corrected = R9 frozen, @bc3c381), v4.1.5 (R10, @89f5840) and v4.1.6 (Causa, @dae2347). Post-hoc ablation: the R8-INV04 catch survives all five C1 variants, but a naive emission rule adds a T-S47 'automatic reads pause' false alarm on every control, and dropping the remaining-budget repeatability rule adds T-S14 and T-S65 alarms on every control. Both rules were chosen after viewing those control rows.
findings.limitations: Three control packages share ancestry with the target (successive amendments of one specification); no independent specification was available. Not a blind control.

findings.title: C2's name-based rule does not generalise out of sample
findings.statement: Post-hoc probe over six other Echelon F# source trees (causa src @97c0a98, time-entry f-sharp @c120ada, vigila, signal, strata, ordo): 12 alarms in 3 trees, none judged a real defect by the author: 5 per-command records in time-entry (the type itself names the command), a capability descriptor in causa, and 6 CLI/receipt cases in ordo carrying command names as strings. A generic version must restrict candidates to the parameter type of an operation that must accept several commands (e.g. Decide), which was not tested.
findings.limitations: Author adjudication, unreviewed; the trees are implementation code, not frozen packages.

findings.title: Cycle-level C1 (secondary) is noisy because invariant preconditions are not modelled
findings.statement: C1-cycle raises 6 alarms on each control package and 2 extra on R8: the cycle T-S19/T-S58/T-S59 (schedule read 1) -> T-S22 (ReconcileMarkerBytesMatch) -> T-S04 (SaveRequested) emits a read per save. That cycle needs a successful read, so it cannot occur 'under total network failure', which C1 does not evaluate. The self-loop restriction of the primary variant is what removes them.
findings.limitations: 18 control alarms counted as false positives per the preregistration.

findings.title: Causa T18->T20 dependency was derivable from pre-T0 artifacts; B2's 'not in any pre-T0 artifact' is contradicted
findings.statement: In the pre-T0 Causa inputs (@dae2347, before T0 2026-11-07T16:10:50Z), SL-T18's acceptance tests include playwright:invariants/INV-21.spec.js; v4/invariants.json INV-21 lists sources EXT-DATA-004 and EXT-DATA-005; the slice manifest assigns both to SL-T20 ('Connect flow and GitHub provider'), which declares dependsOn SL-T18. C4 (implied edge test -> invariant -> source requirement -> owning slice) therefore yields SL-T18->SL-T20 and the 2-cycle T18<->T20 that Causa's FINAL-REPORT names (INV-21.spec.js drives Connect, wired only by T20). B2 checked the test's obligations (PF-015-O4, owned by T18) rather than the invariant's sources. Classification refers to B2's claim (contradicted); the dependency link is VERIFIED from the artifacts.
findings.limitations: As a detector it is noisy: the same SCC on Causa also holds T16<->T22 and T19<->T22 two-cycles (INV-24/INV-13/INV-25), and the R10 control yields a 6-slice SCC (T16, T17, T19, T22, WI-GEN-EXT-DATA, WI-GEN-UI). Neither can be adjudicated: Causa never got past T18, and R10 merged under owner rule B after its gate deadlock. C4-all gives 25-29-slice SCCs. Designed after knowing the answer.

findings.title: C3 (exploratory) flags the DEV-R8-12 missing transition on R8 only
findings.statement: C3 flags (UnknownOutcome, ReconcileReadFailed) in v4.1.1, whose only transition T-S29 is guarded 'fewer than three automatic reads made' and has no exhausted-budget transition (the stall DEV-R8-12 recorded). 0 alarms on all controls, where T-S64 covers it.
findings.limitations: Not in the brief's blocker list; answer-informed; lexical guard classification.

findings.title: Cost: under one second for all four packages
findings.statement: Loading and running every check on four packages takes 0.26-0.63 s in-process (0.33-0.72 s process wall) on the shared host at load average 9-11; each check is <=0.02 s per package. No build is needed.
findings.limitations: Excludes design effort, which here was guided by the known answer.

findings.title: Prior art already covers these defects
findings.statement: Indy-init records that 'percepta spec-preflight', introduced for R9 after R8, exits 3 on v4.1.1 in 0.3 s, finding INV-04 x T-S31/T-S32, the CommandEnvelope discrimination gap and the (UnknownOutcome, ReconcileReadFailed) gap, and passes on v4.1.2; it is wired into preflight-tooling.yml for v4.1.5. B3 did not re-run it. Like B3's checks it was built knowing the answer.
findings.limitations: Documentary only.

findings.title: Indy-init's spec-preflight claim reproduces exactly
findings.statement: percepta spec-preflight 0.4.0 (4a53688, the version Indy-init pinned for R9 and the competition) exits 3 on frozen v4.1.1 (R8) in 5/5 runs, median 0.34 s, with exactly the documented findings: 2 blocking likely-contradictions (INV-04 x SM-SAVE T-S31, T-S32), 1 blocking missing-interface (CommandEnvelope cannot discriminate 134 catalog commands; body lost through 7 carrier types), 2 non-blocking missing-specifications ((UnknownOutcome, ReconcileReadFailed) = DEV-R8-12; (UnknownOutcome, CheckAgain)). On v4.1.2, v4.1.5 and v4.1.6 it exits 0 with zero findings of any kind (median 0.26-0.35 s).
limitations: Local rebuild from tagged source (percepta --version: 0.4.0), not the downloaded release archive.
Wall time includes process start on a host at load 9-11.

findings.title: R9 pin = HEAD; the first spec-preflight commit gives identical results
findings.statement: Indy-init kickoff/rehearsal-009/toolchain.lock.json (bc3c381) expects percepta-semantic 0.4.0; docs/competition-readiness/dependency-lock.json (dae2347) pins tag percepta-semantic-v0.4.0 at commit 4a53688, which is the percepta clone's HEAD. The first spec-preflight commit 0ad2bd3 differs only in one at-limit regex and produces byte-identical reports on all 8 package x condition cells.
limitations: 0ad2bd3 run n=3.

findings.title: Per-defect agreement with B3: both catch the two R8 blockers and DEV-R8-12; only B3 sees T18<->T20
findings.statement: R8-INV04: B3 C1-loop CAUGHT, spec-preflight CAUGHT. R8-CMDBODY: B3 C2 CAUGHT, spec-preflight CAUGHT (DOC condition). DEV-R8-12: B3 C3 (exploratory) FLAGGED, spec-preflight reports it (non-blocking). Causa T18<->T20: B3 C4 DETECTABLE (noisy), spec-preflight cannot see it: it takes no slice/plan input and reports nothing on v4.1.6.
evidence: research/2026-11-08-compute-sprint/tracks/B4-preflight/B3 results.csv (worker 82f159b), re-run from scratch copy: identical
limitations: The T18<->T20 result for spec-preflight is by construction (out of scope), not a measured miss of a capable rule.

findings.title: False alarms: spec-preflight 0 on every control; fewer extras on R8 than B3
findings.statement: Controls v4.1.2/v4.1.5/v4.1.6: spec-preflight 0 blocking and 0 non-blocking findings each. B3: primary checks 0 each; secondary C1-cycle 6 per control (18 total); C4 one 6-slice cycle group on R10 and Causa. On R8, spec-preflight's only extra is the non-blocking (UnknownOutcome, CheckAgain) pair (documented upstream as plausibly intended); B3 C1-loop adds 3 misattributions to the per-request 'three automatic reads' clause plus T-S47 (judged related-true by B3 post hoc), which spec-preflight does not flag (its effect matcher needs the whole phrase 'reconciliation read'; T-S47 says 'one read on return').
limitations: Controls share ancestry and were seen by both tool authors; zero false alarms here says little about other specifications.

findings.title: Indy-init's CI invocation drops the carrier check
findings.statement: Indy-init .github/workflows/preflight-tooling.yml (dae2347) runs spec-preflight on v4.1.5 without --catalog and asserts only blocked==false and empty blockingContradictions. Without the catalog the carrier rule has no carrier to test: on R8 that invocation (CI condition) still exits 3 but does not report the CommandEnvelope defect. The r9.fsx wrapper used in STARTUP passes --catalog and refuses on any blocking section, so it is not affected.
limitations: Only R8 shows the effect; on controls CI and DOC agree (no findings).

findings.title: spec-preflight was built knowing the R8 answer, by the session that also wrote the corrected control
findings.statement: R8 ran on 2026-11-01 (rehearsal-008 commits 17:36Z-23:53Z; DEV-R8-09 18:22Z, DEV-R8-11 18:55Z, DEV-R8-12 23:04Z). spec-preflight's first commit 0ad2bd3 is 2026-11-02 01:23Z; its docs present the R8 package as the regression target and state that two false positives seen on it were fixed. Commits 0ad2bd3, 92527ed, the 0.4.0 release (9c671dc) and Indy-init's R9 handoff, v4.1.2 amendment (2dc5a05) and compiled v4.1.2 (f24b167, 19:31Z, after 92527ed) all carry the same Claude-Session trailer. 92527ed was tuned on draft v4.1.2 wording; the frozen v4.1.2 also passes the pre-fix build. v4.1.5 (2026-11-06) and v4.1.6 (2026-11-07) post-date the release, but v4.1.5 was gated by the tool in CI.
limitations: Same session trailer shows shared authorship context, not intent to overfit.

findings.title: Neither tool is shown to be generic; both are lexically tuned
findings.statement: Post-hoc rewrites of R8 that keep each defect: spec-preflight misses INV-04 when the bound says 'no more than ... in any 60-second window' (P1), when the loop is a 2-cycle (P3) or the effect is reworded (P4), and misses the carrier gap when CommandEnvelope gains an irrelevant string field (P5) or the catalog says 'travels in' instead of 'is carried inside' (P6); it survives 'per minute' (P2) and renaming the carrier (P7). B3 C1-loop misses P3 and P4 and on P1 alarms only through the wrong clause; C1-cycle survives P3; B3 C2 survives P5-P7 only because it keys on type and field names containing 'Command'. No requirement id is hard-coded in spec-preflight's rules (grep), but its trigger vocabulary ('at most N X in T seconds', 'carried inside', 'spent', 'already made|sent|used|done') matches this specification family.
limitations: Post hoc, adversarially chosen probes on one package; false-alarm behaviour on independent specifications is untested for both tools.

findings.title: The counter-coverage rule conflates counters, so a finding can disappear without the gap being closed
findings.statement: (UnknownOutcome, CheckAgain) has transitions only under 'automatic reads spent' in v4.1.1 and in v4.1.2/v4.1.5 alike, so the side with automatic reads left is unspecified in all of them. spec-preflight reports it on v4.1.1 but not on v4.1.2, because v4.1.2's guards add 'fewer than four reconciliation reads ... in the 60 s' (a different counter), which satisfies the below-limit regex. Whether failing closed there is intended remains an owner question.
limitations: Single instance; the missing side may well be intended.

findings.title: Echelon should reuse spec-preflight for C1/C2/C3-class checks rather than build new ones
findings.statement: On the four packages, spec-preflight matches B3's two primary catches and C3, with no control false alarms of any kind, fewer R8 extras, comparable cost (about 0.3 s, no build at use since it ships as a released self-contained CLI), and it is already pinned and wired into Indy-init's r9.fsx/STARTUP gate. B3's C1-loop/C2/C3 duplicate it. B3's distinct value is C4 (slice-dependency cycles), and C1-cycle as a 2-cycle extension; those could be proposed as additions to the percepta module rather than a parallel tool. Indy-init's CI step should pass --catalog and check every blocking section.
limitations: Recommendation, not a measurement; generality of both tools is unproven (B4-F-07).

findings.title: The library and tool ecosystem runs on a release set 35 versions behind the approved one
findings.statement: 23 of 33 inspected repositories install Praxis 3.7.2 (.echelon/ros.json) and 23 carry the Ordo 1.5.0 .sde payload; 15 bind Conditor authority to echelon-current 1.2.0 and 9 more to sets 1.3.0-1.24.0. The approved set is 1.37.0 (Praxis 3.25.0, Ordo 1.20.0). The Registry, Dokimos, Limen, Forma, Percepta, Aegis and Tutela repositories, which produce the approved set, are themselves on 1.2.0. Only causa and indy-init-rehearsal-010 match the approved set. Of 375 consumer version pins, 169 match the approved selection, 200 are behind, 3 are ahead (unqualified) and 3 have no approved counterpart.
findings.limitations: Pins describe what each repository declares on main; a few repositories may run newer tools locally. 'minor-behind' groups every same-major gap (3.7.2 to 3.25.0 counts as one class).

findings.title: Released Praxis capabilities are unreachable in most repositories
findings.statement: Because 23 repositories run Praxis 3.7.2 in CI (./praxis installs the pinned version: praxis-validation.yml), features released in 3.8-3.25 (inbox claim lifecycle 3.8.0, work finish / attested completion 3.20.0, requirements manifest 3.25.0) cannot run there. The program builds capabilities faster than the ecosystem adopts them.
findings.limitations: Capability-to-version mapping taken from CURRENT-STATE and Registry notes, not re-executed.

findings.title: Two catalogs of qualified versions force a Conditor release for most component releases
findings.statement: Conditor embeds its own component registry (components/*.component.json: 11 descriptors with qualifiedVersions and defaultVersion; src/Conditor.Core/Registry.fs) alongside the echelon-registry catalog (17 systems). REG-RU-007 requires a released Conditor to qualify each set, so 13 Conditor releases (v0.10.9-v0.10.21) accompanied 12 approved sets (1.26.0-1.37.0) in 14 days; commits for 0.10.15-0.10.20 are literally 'Request Conditor 0.10.X (qualifies echelon-current 1.Y.0) - RELEASE TRIGGER'. The catalogs disagree: Conditor has forma-workflow (not in the Registry); the Registry has dokimos, arca, fides, strata, summa-contracts, limen-fsharp, percepta-semantic (no Conditor descriptor).
findings.limitations: Release counts from tag commit dates; some Conditor releases also carried feature work (e.g. ci-policy, unattended-readiness).

findings.title: The designed escape from per-version qualification is built but switched off
findings.statement: Conditor implements attested range qualification (Registry.attestedQualification, src/Conditor.Core/Registry.fs:21-26) but trusts no Registry release-attestation key (trust/registry-release-keys.json:4 'keys': []), so every project binding stays exact-version qualified. CURRENT-STATE (2026-10-23) already noted empty trust keys; nothing changed.
findings.limitations: Whether range qualification would be acceptable to the owner is a policy question.

findings.title: Praxis duplicates Ordo contract admission because it pins an Ordo.Core that predates it
findings.statement: Praxis.Domain references EchelonFoundry.Ordo.Core 1.8.2 from vendor/nuget (Praxis.Domain.fsproj:6-9) and carries its own 1,043-line Ordo model and contract admission that reproduce Ordo's ORDO.CONTRACT.* vocabulary (ContractAdmission.fs:7-9). Ordo 1.20.0 source defines that module (src/Ordo.Core/ConstructibilityContract.fs:77). The vendored 1.8.2 DLL contains no 'Constructibility' type names (strings scan of lib/*/Ordo.Core.dll).
findings.limitations: Behavioural equivalence of the two implementations not tested; Ordo 1.20.0's package contents not inspected (only source).

findings.title: Iter is an unused duplicate of Limen.Routing
findings.statement: Iter (typed F# routing, unreleased, Registry readiness 'not-ready') has zero incoming edges in the dependency graph. EchelonFoundry.Limen.Routing provides F# routing and URL state, is released in limen-fsharp 0.9.0 and is consumed by praxis, chrona, signal and summa.
findings.limitations: Iter's design intent (application-side primitives beyond routing) is broader than routing; only routing exists.

findings.title: Profile-'required' components are not installed on the product path
findings.statement: echelon-current marks 12 components required, including dokimos, tutela, visual-engineering, communication-engineering and percepta-semantic. causa and indy-init-rehearsal-010 (the only repositories on the approved set) pin none of these in conditor.json. Tutela is installed in only fides and iter; Dokimos is pinned only by fides (0.2.0) and reaches CI through three different routes. 'required' is therefore descriptive, not enforced.
findings.limitations: The Registry may intend 'required' to mean 'part of the environment' rather than per-repository; no spec text defining per-repository enforcement was found.

findings.title: Aegis 2.0.0 is documented but has never been released
findings.statement: Aegis source is 2.0.0 ('Release 2.0.0: fail-closed store queries', ec0e876, 2026-10-05) and docs/aegis/README.md:203 describes it as a major release, but the repository has no tags, the Registry knows only 1.0.0 (nuget), and all 16 consumers use 1.0.0. Unchanged since the 2026-10-23 inventory; the repository's last commit is 2026-10-16.
findings.limitations: NuGet.org was not queried directly; Registry record used as the release source.

findings.title: forma-workflow is installed and qualified outside the Registry
findings.statement: Causa pins forma-workflow 1.2.0 in conditor.json without a registryAuthority; Conditor qualifies it as a built-in component (8313de7, 2026-11-06); the Registry catalog has no forma-workflow system. Forma Studio separately vendors Forma.Workflow source at 1.1.0.
findings.limitations: None material.

findings.title: Unqualified Limen F# 0.9.1 is in use
findings.statement: Specula references EchelonFoundry.Limen.Contract and Limen.Guest 0.9.1; the Registry states 'Limen F# stays at 0.9.0 (its 0.9.1 was not qualified)'. Specula has no conditor.json, so no governance check sees it.

findings.statement: Chrona, Signal and Summa pin Arca 0.5.0; the Registry records that Chrona does not compile against 0.6.0+ and stays on echelon-current 1.31.0. Fides.Arca still targets Arca.Core 0.1.0.

findings.title: The program repository has grown a parallel toolchain
findings.statement: Indy-init holds about 39,000 lines of tooling under tools/; requirements-compiler alone is 16,040 lines of F# with Ledger, Continuation, TokenEconomics, Observer, VerificationPlan and Graph modules, reading Praxis's on-disk event logs and execution records directly. findings.title: No repository scans dependencies for known vulnerabilities
findings.statement: Across the workflows of 31 Echelon repositories plus Indy-init and rehearsal-010 there is no CodeQL, dependency review, npm audit, `dotnet list package --vulnerable`, OSV or Dependabot configuration. Nine repositories attest build provenance; Tutela (security engineering) is installed in two.

findings.title: READMEs misstate responsibility or installed versions
findings.statement: Summa's README describes a 'project-administration hub' while the code is an invoicing ledger (CONTRADICTED by code). Dokimos says security is owned by 'Aegis/Tutors' (Aegis is fault handling; no 'Tutors' exists). Ordo, Signal, Chrona, Vigila, Folio, Communication Engineering and echelon-foundry READMEs state ROS/Praxis versions 1.2.1-3.7.1 that differ from what .echelon/ros.json installs. Aegis docs describe an unreleased 2.0.0.
findings.limitations: Only README/top-level docs were compared.

findings.statement: observer is empty; census (financial ledger, AWS/PostgreSQL) and armamentarium (signed build kit) are documentation-only; vitium is a proposed baseline with unconsumed preview packages. Census's ledger overlaps Summa.Ledger, armamentarium overlaps Conditor plus Registry, and Vitium overlaps Dokimos/Specula by stated scope. Limen.Outbox overlaps Arca's offline queue.

findings.title: Approval churn: 12 owner-approved release sets in 13 days
findings.statement: echelon-current advanced from 1.26.0 (2026-10-24) to 1.37.0 (2026-11-05), almost one owner approval per day, mostly to admit one or two component bumps for the next Indy rehearsal. Combined with C-F-03, a single component release costs a component release, a Conditor release, a Registry set and an owner approval.
findings.limitations: Owner time per approval not measured.

findings.title: Attestations are per release, ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 over a four-field statement, not signatures over a Registry set
findings.statement: A signed resolved-set component entry must carry systemId, version, role 'project-binding', releaseManifest.sha256 and a releaseAttestation {schema 'echelon.release-attestation/v1', algorithm 'ecdsa-p256-sha256', keyId, base64 signature, non-empty consumerContracts including 'echelon.web-package-binding/v1'}. The signed payload is the UTF-8 line 'echelon.release-attestation/v1|systemId|version|releaseManifestSha256|sorted contracts'; the signature is IEEE P1363 r||s, verified with the BCL against a DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo P-256 key from the embedded trust file. Nothing signs the set as a whole; CR-01's 'sign Registry sets' wording is inaccurate.
findings.limitations: Spec text describes the Registry side that does not exist yet; verified against Conditor code and our signer only.

findings.title: With a valid attestation the built-in catalog need not list the version, but must still declare a qualifiedRange for that component
findings.statement: Conditor qualifies a version absent from qualifiedVersions when the descriptor declares qualifiedRange containing it, the version is not in deniedVersions, and the attestation verifies and claims the web contract. Shown on the production trust path with only the trust file changed: real echelon-current 1.37.0 forma 0.13.0 with 0.13.0 removed from the catalog, and synthetic forma 0.14.0 on the stock v0.10.21 catalog, both pass attestedSelections, Compatibility.validateIn and CLI `conditor doctor` (no COND-DOC-COMPAT), while the same unsigned set is refused. The production CurrentUpgrade.preview/apply (upgrade --current) qualifies Forma 0.7.0 as 'attested:>=0.2.0 <1.0.0:test-only-c2-001-2026-11-08' and applies it with no drift.
findings.limitations: A4 full apply used the existing fixture repo (Forma 0.6.1->0.7.0 with fake npm), not 1.37.0 data; doctor exited 12 in both arms for unrelated lifecycle findings.

findings.title: The range-qualification code is live, reachable from the CLI's normal flows
findings.statement: The embedded trust is consumed by Planner.create (init/verify/doctor/status/repair/upgrade via Program.fs:90 and Doctor.fs:73), Compatibility.validateIn (Doctor.fs:63) and CurrentUpgrade.preview/apply (Program.fs:706,734; WebPackageBinding plan/verify at CurrentUpgrade.fs:379-384,442-444). It is dormant only because the trust list is empty, not dead code; populating the trust file activated it end to end through the CLI binary.
findings.limitations: Scaffolding without a Registry authority (EmbeddedCatalog) still pins from descriptor data only (Scaffolding.fs:53-69).

findings.title: Bad attestations are refused with clear reasons; an expiry/replay-by-date control does not exist
findings.statement: Refused (NotAttested with a reason, not selected): one hex char of the signed manifest digest changed ('signature does not verify'), one signature byte flipped (same), untrusted key under the pinned keyId (same; also refused by production preview with that reason), untrusted key under an unknown keyId ('is not pinned'), revoked key ('was revoked at ...'), another version's statement replayed ('does not verify'), wrong contract (attested but not selected), out-of-range 1.0.0 (not selected), host-tool praxis (not selected). The format carries no expiry or freshness: an 'expiresAt' in the past is ignored and the attestation stays valid indefinitely; revocation needs a Conditor release (REG-SIG-007).
findings.limitations: N6 used a stand-in digest for the replayed 0.12.0 statement; no real historical attestations exist.

findings.title: The attestation does not cover the rest of the set entry (artifact digests, URLs)
findings.statement: Changing one hex char of an unsigned field (artifacts[0].sha256) leaves the attestation valid (S1). Integrity of those fields rests on the set digest: a recorded authority altered after its digest was recorded is ignored (S3), and upgrade targets require a caller-supplied set digest; the digest itself is not signed. CR-01 therefore gives contract-claim authenticity, not set integrity.
findings.limitations: Whether the release-manifest digest chain covers artifact digests on the Registry side was not traced.

findings.title: Populating the trust file breaks exactly one existing check, the deliberate 'inert' guard
findings.statement: Full suite on 528ef45: R0 1552 PASS / 0 FAIL; with the TEST-ONLY key in the trust file R1 1552 PASS / 1 FAIL; with the added embedded-trust scenario R1k 1557 PASS / 1 FAIL. The only failure is 'this build pins no Registry release key yet, so contract qualification is inert until the Registry signs' (DeclaredWebBindingTests.fs:900-902), which a real enablement release would invert.
findings.limitations: Suite is a custom check runner (PASS/FAIL lines), counted by grep.

findings.title: CR-01 would not end lockstep Conditor releases: 2 of 13 recent releases were avoidable
findings.statement: Range qualification is limited to project-binding web packages whose descriptor declares qualifiedRange (forma, limen, folio, forma-workflow); descriptors for host-tool and lifecycle components may not declare a range (CON-343). In echelon-current 1.37.0 only 3 of 17 entries are range-eligible. Of Conditor v0.10.9-v0.10.21, 2 (v0.10.15, v0.10.17: Forma-only) were avoidable, 9 were required (7 add Praxis/Ordo host-tool versions, v0.10.10 changes folio releaseArtifacts, v0.10.21 adds a new descriptor), 2 changed no catalog. The claim 'that would end the lockstep Conditor releases' is contradicted; the dominant driver is Praxis/Ordo.
findings.limitations: Classification is from catalog diffs only; some releases also carried feature work. v0.10.10 (folio releaseArtifacts) is arguably avoidable for Registry-authority repos, giving at most 3/13.

findings.title: CR-01 needs new infrastructure and process on the Registry side
findings.statement: The Registry has no trust/release-signing-keys.json, no signing workflow or protected environment, no resolver step copying releaseAttestation, and no REG-SIG conformance checks; WI-0042 (implement REG-SIG) is 'ready, proposal-required' pending a key-custody proposal. Its REG-RU-007 gate reads only exact versions from `conditor compatibility --json` and refuses a range-only forma 0.14.0 on all 5 platforms ('Release a Conditor that qualifies these versions'), so it must change too. Key rotation and revocation each still require a Conditor release.
