findings.title: Default work completion accepts any existing file as 'tests' evidence, and no surveyed repository enables verified completion
findings.statement: With the default scaffold ros.json, `praxis work complete --evidence implementation=README.md --evidence tests=/etc/hostname --conclusion 'all tests pass'` moves the item to complete. The check only confirms that the evidence types are present and the paths exist. Nothing runs, parses or binds the evidence to a revision, and the path may be outside the repository. `praxis verify` exits 0 and `work validate` reports valid with 0 findings afterwards. None of the 45 ros.json files surveyed (16 local repositories, 29 ext clones) sets requireVerifiedCompletion, requireAttestedEvidence or trustedVerifierKeyIds, and docs/verified-completion-rollout.md confirms that verified completion is not enabled anywhere. Every 'complete' state in the ecosystem is therefore self-declared. A durable-checkpoint guard applies only when the work changed tracked files, and it requires a commit, a push and a checkpoint, not a test run.
findings.limitations: Tested on the default scaffold policy only. Repository-specific quality policies (QualityEvidencePolicy) can raise the required evidence types, but they do not make the evidence verifiable.

findings.title: Indy-init acceptance verifier returns ACCEPTED for a fully fabricated evidence bundle when the manifest digest comes from the bundle's producer, as in rehearsal-005's acceptance.sh
findings.statement: The verifier checks internal consistency: digests, run_id, source_sha, schema, and that each artifact says status PASS with exit_code 0 and a non-empty 'command' string. It cannot tell whether any command ran. Its 'independently pinned' --evidence-manifest-sha256 is, in rehearsal-005 tools/acceptance/ci/acceptance.sh, the stdout of the candidate's own `causa-acceptance ledger` step in the same job. --trusted-source-sha is the candidate's SOURCE_SHA. A script inside my track wrote 118 artifacts (G0-G9 plus all 108 P0 requirements of the real baseline BL-CAUSA-INDY-INIT-aab8f80c7743, sha256 621e2f96...) with `command: 'echo fabricated'`. Run against the real rehearsal-005 approvals (3e70dcd2...), for a candidate repository holding only README.md, the verifier exited 0 with verdict ACCEPTED, no reasons and no claim problems. The workflow, the acceptance.sh pins and the producer tool all live in the candidate repository, and no repository has CODEOWNERS or branch protection (E-F-07). The agent under evaluation therefore controls the pipeline that judges it. This generalises cohort-based-engineering's 'Rehearsal 2 self-declared; INVALID' correction: the later rehearsals' 'computed' verdicts are only as independent as the CI that computes them.
findings.limitations: Only the ledger verifier was exercised. Rehearsal-005 also runs `requirements-compiler verify-plan`, which checks test identity against result files; those files are candidate-produced too, but I did not test them. Not tested against GitHub (local fixture only).

findings.title: The claim-ownership guard on plain completion is removed by deleting the out-of-tree claim record
findings.statement: For a claimed item, plain `work complete` is refused with PRX.COMPLETION.VERIFIED_COMPLETION_REQUIRED (exit 3). After `rm -rf $(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/praxis/claims/<ID>`, the same command completes the item (exit 0) with fabricated evidence. The local store is writable by the completing process and is not a trust root, which the docs state for the verifier re-read but not for this guard.
findings.limitations: Requires local write access to the Git directory, which an implementation agent normally has.

findings.title: The 'protected' completion policy is read from local refs: moving refs/remotes/origin/main or rewriting history defeats it
findings.statement: Controls hold for direct weakening. NX-3: committing a ros.json that drops requireVerifiedCompletion is refused with PRX.COMPLETION.POLICY_CHANGED. NX-6a: a weakening commit with no remote is also POLICY_CHANGED. NX-5a: a keyless authority is ATTESTATION_REQUIRED. They are defeated by local ref manipulation with no push. NX-4: `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main HEAD` lets plain completion succeed. NX-5B: the same plus forged result and event completes as 'verified' under a policy that required attestation. NX-6B: an orphan-root history rewrite in a repository without a remote also completes as 'verified'. docs/verified-completion-rollout.md lists this as a known limit. This experiment confirms it still holds on 3.25.0. The host-side post-hoc audit the docs prescribe is the only mitigation, and I found no implementation of it in the repositories.
findings.limitations: Documented residual risk, so severity is held at Medium. Local fixtures only.

findings.title: Non-attested verified completion succeeds with zero evidence through a caller-chosen authority
findings.statement: The authority file is supplied by the caller. An authority with RequiredValidationNames [] and RequiredEvidenceIds [] makes `work complete-verified` record a Dokimos-accepted completion with evidenceDigests [] and attestation 'unattested'. It also writes a 'praxis: verified completion of NX-7' metadata commit. No forgery is needed: the 'verified' label certifies only that the caller's own requirements, here none, were met. REL-001 GATE-5 (`validate-run -- true`) is the related case where the agent chooses the test command. On 3.25.0 it still verifies.
findings.limitations: No surveyed repository uses this mode today (E-F-01). The docs already state that unattested mode is forgeable.

findings.title: Regression: Praxis 3.25.0 / Dokimos 0.11.1 refuse every attested-mode forgery and the evidence-binding attacks (controls working)
findings.statement: The REL-001 gate script v319, last run on 3.19.0, was re-run unchanged on 3.25.0 and all 17 cases matched. Refused: GATE-1 and GATE-2 (EVIDENCE_UNRECOGNIZED), GATE-3U (EVIDENCE_UNRECORDED), GATE-4 (EVIDENCE_NOT_PASSED), A1 (RECEIPT_MISSING; derived form EVIDENCE_MISSING), A2 (RECEIPT_UNTRUSTED_KEY), A2B (RECEIPT_INVALID_SIGNATURE), A3 (RECEIPT_NOT_PASSED), A5 (POLICY_CHANGED) and A6 (UNTRUSTED_AUTHORITY). A4, a genuine receipt, verified with keyids matching the host verifier. GATE-3, the non-attested forged result plus event, still verifies, as documented. My additional case NX-8, evidence from revision A cited at revision B, was refused with PRX.COMPLETION.HEAD_MISMATCH and ARGUMENT_MISMATCH. The cohort's v3.19.0 results were stale relative to 3.25.0; they are now refreshed.
findings.limitations: The verifier daemon ran as the same OS user, so key isolation was not tested.

findings.title: No branch protection or CODEOWNERS on the repositories whose protected branch every gate assumes, and the agent credential is reported as admin
findings.statement: VERIFIED parts: the GitHub API (list_branches, read-only) reports main protected=false for kemiller2002/praxis, and every listed branch of causa-acceptance-r10 is protected=false. None of praxis, ordo, Indy-init or rehearsals 001-010 has a CODEOWNERS file. SUPPORTED parts, from indy-init-audits rehearsal-007 sub-audit 3 at 10aeded: the session's GitHub App user-to-server token has admin on every kemiller2002 repository; agent merges appear under the owner's login; no rulesets exist; and the agent holds the P-256 authorization signing key and chooses its own trust store (F1, rated critical, accepted, not closed). Consequently E-F-02, E-F-04 and the workflow-file pins (INDY_INIT_REF, APPROVALS_SHA256, OPERATOR) are all agent-modifiable.
findings.limitations: The `protected` flag in the branches API may not reflect every ruleset configuration, and I could not read rulesets or settings (read-only; no settings API). Repositories outside the session allowlist, such as dokimos, were not queryable.

findings.title: Rehearsal owner and reviewer attestations identify the owner only by GitHub review login
findings.statement: ReviewAttestations.fs turns any APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED or DISMISSED review into an attestation keyed by review.user.login, and ProcessVerification matches that login against the frozen owner and reviewer logins. Nothing checks how the review was authored (for example, via an app or token). Per E-F-07, the agent's credential acts as the owner's user. If PRs are authored by a different identity, an agent-submitted review satisfies the owner attestation. The design itself, observing reviews from the API inside the run, is sound against forged files.
findings.limitations: Not executed: testing would require submitting reviews on GitHub, which is out of scope.

findings.title: Release attestation verification binds only the repository, not the workflow or ref; attest-and-publish can run from any branch via workflow_dispatch
findings.statement: native-release.yml has workflow-level contents:write, id-token:write and attestations:write, and accepts workflow_dispatch on any ref. Its attest and publish steps are gated only by event_name != pull_request and 'version not yet published'. Consumers run `gh attestation verify FILE --repo REPO` without --signer-workflow, --source-ref or --cert-identity. A build of an unreviewed branch dispatched by any writer, including the agent per E-F-07, would yield attestations that consumers accept. NuGet publishing in the same job uses NuGet/login@v1, pinned by tag, while holding an OIDC token that can be exchanged for a nuget.org key. The same tag-pinned pattern appears in dokimos, aegis, fides, arca and vitium. praxis-bootstrap.sh also treats a local cache file containing 'verified' as proof of a past attestation check.
findings.limitations: No workflow was dispatched (prohibited). Whether the nuget.org trusted-publishing policy restricts the ref was not observable.

findings.title: CI hygiene: 821 tag-pinned action references (38 SHA-pinned), 2 workflows without permissions, dispatch inputs interpolated into shell
findings.statement: 817 first-party and 4 third-party (NuGet/login@v1) `uses:` references are tag-pinned. Only 38 are SHA-pinned (attest-build-provenance, create-github-app-token, echelon reusable workflows). praxis-validation.yml and Indy-init preflight-tooling.yml have no permissions block, so they get the default token permissions. `${{ inputs.* }}` is interpolated directly into run: scripts in rehearsal-006 acceptance-final.yml and acceptance-process.yml, Indy-init live-provider-preflight.yml, and conditor remote-bootstrap.yml and remote-execute-codex.yml (which also holds id-token:write). acceptance-process.yml interpolates `inputs.candidate` into the very step meant to validate it. These triggers are workflow_dispatch only, so exploitation requires write access. Three workflows use privileged triggers. praxis-reconcile-apply.yml (pull_request_target, contents:write) builds the CLI from the trusted base, restricts to same-repo PRs and passes head.ref through env, which is good practice. The deploy-pages workflow_run workflows in rehearsals 003 and 004 check out the triggering head_sha only for push events. No `github.event.*` attacker-controlled text was found in run steps.
findings.limitations: Static analysis only. Reusable workflow internals and composite actions under ./.github/actions were not expanded.

findings.title: A hand-edited queue.json status 'complete' is not detected
findings.statement: Setting an item's status to 'complete' directly in .ros/work/queue.json, with no transition or event, leaves `praxis verify` at exit 0 and `work validate` valid with 0 findings, and `work show` reports status 'complete'. The live work state in `status --json` does not list the item as complete, so the forgery affects backlog views and any consumer that reads queue.json.
findings.limitations: None noted.

findings.title: Agents can record 'owner-approval' process evidence under a self-declared human identity (labelled unattested)
findings.statement: `work evidence --kind owner-approval --actor-kind human --actor kemiller2002 --outcome approved` run by an agent was accepted (exit 0). Praxis records provenance.class 'owner-decision' with authenticity 'unattested' and basis 'self-reported', so the record itself is honest. The risk lies with downstream consumers that filter on class or kind and ignore authenticity.
findings.limitations: Consumers of these records were not exhaustively audited.

findings.title: No NuGet lock files anywhere, and CI installs tools via curl|sh from a mutable branch
findings.statement: Across 23 audited repositories: 0 packages.lock.json files and RestorePackagesWithLockFile never enabled, so transitive packages are not hash-pinned. Direct versions are exact (0 floating). npm manifests have lockfiles. Praxis and several rehearsals use packageSourceMapping (Praxis maps vendored EchelonFoundry.Ordo/Limen packages to vendor/nuget, which is good). conditor ci.yml (11 places) and percepta run `curl -fsSL .../main/scripts/install-native.sh | sh -s -- --version X`. The version is pinned but the installer bytes come from mutable main, and the installer verifies assets only against a checksum file from the same release (no attestation check).
findings.limitations: Working trees only; no NuGet vulnerability audit was run.

findings.title: Secret scan of 128,562 history blobs in 59 repositories: no live credential identified
findings.statement: 264 pattern hits, 49 of them heuristically live-looking. I manually triaged every live-looking hit, without printing any values. All are test fixtures: header-only private-key marker strings in negative tests (praxis RemoteProtocolTests.fs, summa, arca, cohort fixtures) and synthetic tokens in secret-handling tests (rehearsal-006 AR014Tests.fs, rehearsal-008 connect-save-flow.spec.js, causa, causa-data, dokimos benchmark fixtures). data/secret-scan-redacted.json carries only fingerprints (4-character prefix, length, sha256 prefix).
findings.limitations: Regex and entropy heuristics only. ext/full could not be scanned (not a Git repository).

findings.title: Prompt injection through repository content: none found; agent-isolation gaps recorded by the R7 audit
findings.statement: Pattern scans of praxis, ordo, Indy-init, mercatus, signal, rehearsals 001-010, indy-init-audits, research-documents and 7 ext repos found no content that instructs agents to override instructions or exfiltrate data. Hits were threat-model text describing such attacks and curl|sh install lines. Every checked-out repository's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md is loaded into an agent's context as instructions, by design; they are uniform 'read AGENTS.md' entry points. Separately, the R7 audit recorded that add_repo attached private prior-rehearsal repositories with no owner prompt, so isolation was instruction-only. This session showed the opposite behaviour: the GitHub MCP refused a repository outside the allowlist (dokimos).
findings.limitations: Keyword scan only; obfuscated or semantic injection was not tested.

findings.title: causa-acceptance-r10 is a live-persistence data store written by a dedicated GitHub App, not acceptance machinery
findings.statement: The local clone at e1e7966 holds only README.md. The remote has a 'causa-acceptance' branch and about 30 'causa-live-*' branches of investigation JSON, all committed by causa-acceptance-r10[bot] (a GitHub App, committer GitHub). Attribution through a distinct app identity is a positive control. However, every branch is unprotected (E-F-07), so any holder of a write credential can create commits identical in form.
findings.limitations: The R10 acceptance consumers of this store were not audited.

findings.title: Deriving 'claimed' from the tracked event log refuses the E-F-03 claim-store deletion bypass
findings.statement: With patch praxis-claim-guard-queue-integrity, `work claim` appends a token-free `work.claim.recorded` marker to .ros/events/events.jsonl and plain `work complete` consults the tracked log (working tree ∪ HEAD blob). After `rm -rf <git-common-dir>/praxis/claims/ID`, plain completion is refused with exit 3 and PRX.COMPLETION.CLAIM_RECORD_MISSING (baseline: exit 0). It is still refused when the committed marker's line is also deleted from the working tree (A1b). Normal claim -> validate-run -> complete-verified through real Dokimos 0.11.1 still completes, with and without a commit after the claim; the marker is then committed by the verified-completion metadata commit.
findings.limitations: A1c: if the marker was never committed, deleting it together with the store still bypasses (exit 0). Anyone who can write the repository can forge or rewrite tracked history; the fix moves the bypass into reviewable tracked state, it does not create a trust root. Changes invariant I8; see E2-F-04.

findings.title: A queue/event cross-check detects hand-edited queue.json completions (E-F-11) with no false positives on local repositories
findings.statement: `work validate`, `work backlog-validate` and `validate` now report PRX.QUEUE.UNRECORDED_COMPLETION (exit 1) for a queue row with status 'complete' and no tracked work.completed / work.completion.verified event (baseline: valid, exit 0 on all three). Legitimately completed items produce no finding. A read-only scan of the same rule over 43 local repositories (1881 complete rows) flagged 0.
findings.limitations: Only 'complete' rows are checked: backlog 'abandoned' writes no event in 3.25.0. A forger who also appends a fake work.completed line passes. `praxis verify` is unchanged and still exits 0.

findings.title: Default repository containment plus digest/commit binding refuses /etc/hostname-style evidence (E-F-01) without breaking in-repo completion
findings.statement: With patch praxis-evidence-path, plain `work complete` refuses evidence resolving outside the repository root (absolute, ../ traversal, file symlink, directory symlink) with exit 1 and PRX.EVIDENCE.OUTSIDE_REPOSITORY before any gate, lock or state change; baseline accepted all four. In-repo evidence is accepted and recorded in .ros/work/evidence-bindings.jsonl with sha256 (matches sha256sum) and HEAD commit (matches git rev-parse HEAD) plus committedAtHead. `workProtocol.allowExternalEvidence: true` restores the old behaviour explicitly and still records the digest.
findings.limitations: Proves which bytes at which commit were cited, not that tests ran or passed; a fabricated in-repo log is accepted. praxis init git-ignores logs/, so typical logs bind with committedAtHead=false. Opt-out lives in agent-editable ros.json. Binding is written just before (not inside) the completion transaction.

findings.title: Existing-suite impact: the claim marker conflicts with tests that encode 'claiming never touches the tracked tree'
findings.statement: Baseline suite: 2513 tests, 2511 passed, 2 failed (2035 s). Final patched suite: 2522 tests, 2513 passed, 9 failed (1647 s). Newly failing: 7; all are tests that assert `git status --porcelain` is empty right after `work claim` (invariant I8: claiming never touches the tracked tree). No newly failing test relates to SPR-E2-02. Two baseline failures (real-Dokimos attested end-to-end) are pre-existing.
findings.limitations: Suites ran on a shared 4-vCPU host; timings are indicative. Fixing the conflict needs a design decision (accept a tracked claim marker and update the I8 tests, or commit the marker at claim time), not done here.

findings.title: A verifier-signed evidence flow refuses the E and V2 fabricated bundles that Indy-init's verifier ACCEPTS (local simulation)
findings.statement: Re-running E's and V2's own fabrication scripts against Indy-init dae2347 still yields ACCEPTED from compute-acceptance-verdict.py. The prototype trusted verdict REFUSES both (no verifier signature), refuses a candidate-signed forgery, replay to another commit, tampered entries (with or without a re-hashed manifest) and a dropped entry, ignores a caller-supplied manifest digest, ACCEPTS a genuine run of a correct candidate and FAILS a buggy and a cheating candidate. The candidate uid could not read the key or write the verifier's output (EACCES).
findings.limitations: Local uid separation only. GitHub environment protection, rulesets, required reviewers, OIDC/secrets scoping, runner isolation and the adequacy of acceptance checks for the real 108-requirement baseline are NOT TESTED. Root can bypass everything; in production the agent token must not reach the verifier repo (E-F-07: today it can).

findings.title: Unverified: hardening against an agent with repository write access in general
findings.statement: None of the prototypes protects against an agent that rewrites history, edits tracked logs coherently, or modifies the verifier itself; these require server-side enforcement (protected branches, CODEOWNERS, verifier in an agent-unwritable repo/environment).
findings.limitations: Out of scope of a local prototype.

findings.title: Untrimmed .NET WASM framework dominates payload in R8/R9
findings.statement: Cold-start transfer (uncompressed static server): R8 37.0 MB, R9 27.8 MB, R10 11.1 MB, minimal F# fixture 8.1 MB. R8/R9 set PublishTrimmed=false (BCL assemblies 20.3 MB on disk); R10 uses TrimMode=partial (BCL 2.9 MB).
findings.limitations: Single snapshot per rehearsal; dist sizes include files never fetched (R8 node_modules); 4 vCPU Xeon 2.3 GHz shared container, .NET SDK 10.0.402 (no workloads), headless Chromium 153, measurements/environment.json

findings.title: Time to app-ready in headless Chromium
findings.statement: Localhost cold ready (engine-set marker): fixture 412 ms (n=7, range 296-476), R8 1440 ms (n=7, range 1262-1619), R9 1272 ms (n=7, range 1098-1384), R10 921 ms (n=7, range 756-1082). Emulated 4G with gzip: fixture 3248 ms (n=5, range 3213-3467), R8 13169 ms (n=5, range 13080-13230), R9 9838 ms (n=5, range 9788-9956), R10 5073 ms (n=5, range 4988-5269). Without compression 4G: R8 32003 ms (n=5, range 31950-32141), R10 10294 ms (n=5, range 10210-10444).
findings.limitations: Chromium only; CPU contention from other tracks (loadavg up to 14 on 4 vCPU) inflates localhost numbers; 4G is CDP emulation, not a real network; each app's own ready marker differs in meaning. 4 vCPU Xeon 2.3 GHz shared container, .NET SDK 10.0.402 (no workloads), headless Chromium 153, measurements/environment.json

findings.title: R10's global fetch no-store override defeats HTTP caching of the WASM runtime
findings.statement: R10 boundary.js wraps globalThis.fetch so every GET uses cache: 'no-store' (to keep GitHub reads fresh). The .NET runtime loads _framework assets through fetch, so a warm reload re-downloads 10.1 MB (R9: 0.0 MB, R8: 0.1 MB). Warm 4G ready: R10 9527 ms (n=5, range 9325-9633) vs R9 1291 ms (n=5, range 1048-1300). Root cause: Limen's HttpEffectRequest has no per-request cache mode (0.9.1 and HEAD), so the app patched fetch globally.
findings.limitations: python http.server sends no Cache-Control; R9's warm reuse relies on heuristic caching/revalidation. A CDN with long max-age would not change the no-store behaviour.

findings.title: Full trimming including FSharp.Core cuts R10 payload by about a third
findings.statement: TrimMode=full (+SatelliteResourceLanguages=en) on R10: cold transfer 7.8 MB vs 11.1 MB; FSharp.Core 2.40 -> 0.29 MB; 4G gzip ready 3825 ms (n=5, range 3662-3915) vs 5073 ms (n=5, range 4988-5269). Functional check: R10's own Chromium suite (194 tests, stateful GitHub fake) against the full-trim build, 2 clean runs: 158 pass / 36 fail, the identical failing set as the untrimmed build (3 runs) - no regression detected.
findings.limitations: R10 comment warns that F# reflection formatting (%A) may break under trimming; only paths exercised by the suite are checked.

findings.title: Trimming satellite resources does not change startup
findings.statement: Hypothesis 'removing FSharp.Core satellite resources (0.32 MB, 13 cultures) speeds startup' is contradicted: they are not fetched at startup (cold transfer 11.1 MB vs 11.1 MB); only deploy size changes.
findings.limitations: Invariant-globalization apps only.

findings.title: wasm-tools workload relinking halves the native runtime but is not needed to build
findings.statement: All publishes succeeded without any workload. With wasm-tools installed (isolated SDK copy), R10 publish relinks dotnet.native.wasm 3.00 -> 1.50 MB (total _framework 10.8 -> 9.4 MB); one publish took 83 s vs 34-42 s without (n=1, contended). Startup (clean rerun): localhost 575 ms (n=7, range 528-647) vs R10 921 ms (n=7, range 756-1082); 4G gzip 4086 ms (n=5, range 4053-4127) vs 5073 ms (n=5, range 4988-5269).
findings.limitations: Workload manifest band 10.0.114 may pull a newer runtime pack than 10.0.13; n=1 build.

findings.title: Build and edit-loop cost of F# WASM apps; trimming doubles the edit-publish loop
findings.statement: Release publish of the WASM host (warm NuGet cache). Batch 2 (interleaved, loadavg ~5): cold R8 38.0 s (n=2, range 37.6-38.4), R9 41.4 s (n=3, range 37.7-44.6), R10 36.4 s (n=3, range 36.3-36.7); edit+publish R8 8.2 s (n=2, range 7.9-8.5), R9 5.7 s (n=3, range 5.6-5.9), R10 16.1 s (n=3, range 16.0-16.8). Batch 1 (sequential, loadavg ~12): cold R8 58.1 s (n=3, range 56.7-61.3), R9 46.4 s (n=3, range 39.3-49.1), R10 37.2 s (n=3, range 33.8-42.3); Debug solution build cold R8 32.8 s (n=3, range 30.8-33.0), R9 16.0 s (n=3, range 16.0-21.9), R10 44.6 s (n=3, range 36.7-53.3). All batches pooled: cold R8 56.7 s (n=5, range 37.6-61.3), R9 43.0 s (n=6, range 37.7-49.1), R10 36.6 s (n=6, range 33.8-42.3), fixture 23.2 s (n=3, range 20.4-27.8); no-op 2.5-3.1 s; one-line F# edit then publish: R8 10.2 s (n=5, range 7.9-12.2), R9 6.5 s (n=6, range 5.6-7.5), R10 16.9 s (n=6, range 16.0-17.9), fixture 10.6 s (n=3, range 10.5-12.0). Trimmed apps (R10, fixture: TrimMode=partial) re-run ILLink on every publish, so a one-line edit costs 10.6-16 s versus 5.7-8.2 s for untrimmed R8/R9: the trimming that cuts payload 3-4x (F-F-01) roughly doubles the edit-publish loop; a Debug/no-trim dev loop with Release-only trimming avoids paying both. First-ever publish incl. runtime-pack download: 51.3 s (n=1).
findings.limitations: Heavy contention from concurrent tracks (loadavg median 11.7 on 4 vCPU during batch 1); batch 2 interleaved to reduce order effects; MSBuild node reuse on.

findings.title: Where agents struggle with F#: type mismatches and unresolved names, fixed quickly
findings.statement: 34 agent transcripts (construction-by-design experiments): 123 dotnet build/test/run invocations, 30 failed with F# compiler errors; 202 distinct diagnostics: FS0001 type mismatch 70 (35%), FS0039 undefined name 51 (25%, mostly a module alias used before/without definition), FS0003 value applied as function 22, FS0041 overload resolution 16, FS0072 needs type annotation 11, syntax/offside (FS0010/0058/0604) 13. 18 recovery streaks, median ~0.45 min, max 3.5 min. Conventional arm A: median 7.5 distinct errors/run (0-45, n=12); agent plan arm B: 2 (1-7, n=6); mechanical-first arm C: 0.5 (0-7, n=12).
findings.limitations: Domain-logic tasks, not UI; arms differ in prompt and generated scaffolding, so arm differences are associations; 41 build invocations had undeterminable outcome (output piped/truncated).

findings.title: Compile errors rarely reach rehearsal commits or CI; CI failures are infrastructure
findings.statement: Across 1,236 commits (R1-R10 + causa) only 6 non-merge commits match compile-error terms; FS codes in commit messages appear only in R3 (FS3261 nullness from a leaked Directory.Build.props) and R10 (FS1093 negative-contract tests). R10 Actions: 289 runs, 171 success, 82 cancelled (28%), 36 failed; of 5 sampled failure logs: 2 WebKit/apt download timeouts (15 min each), 1 pinned SDK not installed (exit 155), 1 WebKit-only smoke failure, 1 unidentified.
findings.limitations: Keyword classification is a screen; only 5 CI logs read (token cost); R8 run list is the first 100 of 642.

findings.title: WASM interpreter locals limit is now statically checkable; R8-R10 have ample headroom
findings.statement: scripts/IlFrame.fsx estimates the Mono interpreter tier-0 frame (8 x (args+locals), 16-aligned). It reproduces R5's start failure: View.project 12,683 locals = 101,472 B (limit 65,535) at 5d8888f, max 4,160 B after the fix a0e7d4a. R8/R9/R10 Causa.App max frames 432 / 1,536 / 2,000 B (>=96.9% headroom). R5 lost about 90 min with a non-starting page while CoreCLR unit tests stayed green.
findings.limitations: Value-type locals counted as 8 B (under-count); optimiser retry not modelled.

findings.title: Limen silently drops a second template root, contrary to its docs
findings.statement: Docs (11-api-reference) say a template with more than one root reports BridgeError{phase: binding}. Probe in Chromium with limen 0.9.0 and 0.9.1: data-if and data-each templates with two element roots mount only the first root, kernel 'running', no diagnostic. The same defect recurred in R7 (D-05, hidden relate form) and causa fda2056.
findings.limitations: HEAD (743cdb9) source shows the same firstElementChild check; HEAD not executed.

findings.title: Limen limitations claimed by rehearsal teams: mostly real, two misreadings
findings.statement: Of 6 rehearsal claims: real gaps - no redirect:'manual' on HTTP effects; nested lists not representable (ViewItem primitives; the JS kernel nevertheless renders nested data when fed untyped JSON); measure does not await fonts.ready. Real by design - no beforeunload (bfcache). Misread - 'no LocationChanged for own navigation' is documented behaviour; 'Limen does not manage focus' ignores the optional focus capability shipped in 0.9.0. New: no per-request cache mode (F-F-03).
findings.limitations: fonts.ready claim by code inspection only.

findings.title: Existing contract tooling went unused
findings.statement: Limen 0.9.1 ships view-contract tooling (checkPage/checkProjection/checkEvent, docs/28) that rejects unknown keys, nested lists and non-template data-if; 0 *.view.json files exist in R1-R10 or causa. The Limen focus capability was likewise available but R2 hand-wrote focus handling.
findings.limitations: Adoption barriers not investigated.

findings.title: Folio is declared but not integrated
findings.statement: R10 locks @echelon-foundry/print-components 0.4.1 and lists it in Administration, but its dist ships no Folio asset; the report's print view is hand-written @media print CSS; only the bootstrap print.html uses <ef-print-document>. R8's T30 review recorded the same (Folio only in bootstrap print.html; Report.fs 2 lines).
findings.limitations: R8 later integrated Folio elements (CR-T26); not re-measured.

findings.title: Contrast failures in R10 trace to Forma token pairs; reachable screens pass axe
findings.statement: axe-core 4.14 (WCAG 2.0/2.1 A+AA) on landing/disconnected routes at 1280x800 and 390x844: 0 violations in 22 scans (R8 8, R9 2, R10 10, fixture 2). R10's own suite reports contrast 4.00:1 and 4.39:1 in workspace states (our run reproduces these messages); Forma's catalog/known-issues.json documents exactly --ef-color-text-secondary on --ef-color-surface-secondary 4.0:1 and accent 4.38:1.
findings.limitations: axe only on states reachable without a GitHub session; connected states not scanned by axe directly.

findings.title: Playwright suite stability (Chromium)
findings.statement: r008: 110 chromium tests x 3 runs -> {'stable-pass': 110}; r009: 20 chromium tests x 3 runs -> {'stable-pass': 20}; r010: 194 chromium tests x 3 runs -> {'stable-pass': 158, 'stable-fail': 36}; r010-trimfull: 194 chromium tests x 2 runs -> {'stable-pass': 158, 'stable-fail': 36}. No flaky test in any app. R10's 36 stable failures = 17 live-provider tests (no CAUSA_GITHUB_TOKEN, fail as BLOCKED by design) + 19 acceptance obligations, matching the R10 FINAL-REPORT's list of ~20 known Chromium failures (contrast, save-flow re-read, wording/selector mismatches); PERSIST-031-O19, which R10 called timing-sensitive, passed in all 5 runs. Wall time per R10 run 509-743 s.
findings.limitations: WebKit project unavailable (R8 config includes webkit; excluded). 3 runs per app, serial, under contention.

findings.title: Recurring UI defect patterns and the contracts that would catch them
findings.statement: 29 curated defects (R1-R10, causa) in 11 patterns: contrast/theme 6, focus management 4, responsive/target size 3, Limen template roots 2, WASM interpreter limits 2, build provenance 2, state presentation not derived 2, duplicate structure 2, Folio not integrated 2, test-harness timing 2, F# build config 2. 6/29 were catchable by tools already available (axe 4, Limen focus capability 2), 10/29 partially, 13/29 need a new contract.
findings.limitations: Hand-curated from commit messages and defect files; selection bias towards well-described fixes.

findings.title: Time lost to WASM runtime and deployment issues (estimate)
findings.statement: R4: 19 of 86 commits (22%) are D-HIST-WASM work over 6.2 h of a 13.8 h commit span; R5: ~90 min with a non-starting page; R10: two 15-min WebKit download timeouts and build-and-test cancelled by its 20-min limit once browser suites took ~29 min (R10 final report).
findings.limitations: Commit spans overlap other work; lower/upper bounds not separable.

findings.title: Styling rules worth enforcing automatically
findings.statement: Heuristic lint over app-owned CSS (R1-R10, causa): raw colour literals outside custom properties in R2 (14), R4/R5 (4), R9 (25); rules overriding Forma .ef-* classes 0-25 per app; !important up to 10 (R3); focus outline suppressed 0-2. Forma 0.13 itself hides 9 native controls with opacity 0 (source of causa 3ae3ac9).
findings.limitations: Counts are candidates, not confirmed defects; no causal link measured between lint counts and defects.

findings.title: Every app invents its own app-ready signal
findings.statement: R8 sets html[data-engine=ready], R9 html[data-causa-ready=running], R10 html[data-causa-started-ms] while its suites wait for the 'Loading Causa' status to hide and the title to change. Suites mostly use role locators (R10: 297 getByRole vs 73 CSS locators; R8 168 vs 265; R9 uses 25 test ids) and 3-10 fixed waitForTimeout calls each.
findings.limitations: Static counts only.

findings.title: Agent orchestration plus baseline governance is bundled into existing seats
findings.statement: GitHub includes its cloud coding agent, third-party agents (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Cognition, xAI) via Agent HQ, an agent/model access control plane with audit logging, Code Quality and a metrics dashboard in paid Copilot (Business $19, Enterprise $39 per seat/month). AWS Kiro Teams is $20/seat with SSO, pooled credits and usage limits; Microsoft Foundry and AWS AgentCore sell identity, policy, evaluation and observability as consumption primitives. A standalone 'governed agent platform' from Echelon would compete against features buyers already receive at little or no marginal cost.
findings.limitations: Several GitHub governance features are public preview; enterprise discounts not visible; control-plane depth not hands-on tested.

findings.title: Requirements-first (spec-driven) agent development is now a mainstream bundled feature
findings.statement: Kiro generates requirements.md/design.md/tasks.md, checks requirements for inconsistencies and gaps, executes tasks in dependency waves and offers property-based correctness checks. 'Specs before code' is therefore not a differentiator by itself. What Kiro's docs do not describe is stable requirement IDs carried to a deterministic verification manifest and a tamper-evident preservation gate — which Praxis shipped in 3.21-3.25 (Oct 26-Nov 3, 2026). Echelon's defensible claim is narrower: preservation and verification of every requirement from intake to completion, not spec authoring.
findings.limitations: Absence of traceability features in Kiro is from one docs page, not a hands-on test; Praxis features are released but not yet shown in a customer setting.

findings.title: AI adoption, cost and impact measurement is already a priced, crowded category
findings.statement: Swarmia sells 'AI adoption & cost' as a $5/dev/month add-on and coding-agent metrics for Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code and Codex; LinearB ($29-$59/user/month) sells an AI-vs-human delivery dashboard and policy-as-code for agentic code; Jellyfish sells token-spend monitoring and audit-ready DevFinOps reports; Atlassian completed its DX acquisition (Nov 2025). Echelon's cost telemetry (Praxis price tables, unavailable-not-zero) is not a product wedge; it is useful as an engagement instrument for cost per accepted requirement, a unit these vendors do not advertise.
findings.limitations: Vendor marketing pages; 'cost per accepted requirement' absence among vendors is inferred from pages reviewed, not exhaustive.

findings.title: Developers report a verification/trust gap with AI output
findings.statement: Stack Overflow 2025: 46% distrust vs 33% trust AI accuracy, 3.1% highly trust, 66% cite 'almost right, but not quite'. Stack Overflow 2026: 93% say trusting AI requires source attribution and the most trusted context is project goals and requirements (85%). DORA 2025: AI adoption relates positively to throughput but negatively to delivery stability; 30% report little or no trust in AI code. These document a problem that Echelon's verified-completion and requirement-traceability aim at.
findings.limitations: Self-selected developer surveys (SO recruits via its own channels); DORA ~5,000 respondents, correlational. They show the problem exists among developers, not that budget-holders will pay a third party to solve it.

findings.title: Executives lack evidence that AI investments pay off; cancellations are forecast
findings.statement: McKinsey State of AI 2025 (secondary coverage): 39% report any enterprise EBIT impact from AI, mostly under 5%; 23% scaling agents anywhere, no more than 10% in any one function. Gartner (June 2025) predicts over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by end-2027 owing to cost, unclear value or inadequate risk controls. This now gives citations to Mercatus 2026-09-23 finding 1 (AI value measurement) which had none.
findings.limitations: McKinsey primary page returned 503; Gartner press release 403 (content corroborated across outlets). Gartner figure is a prediction, not a measurement.

findings.title: Regulation is not a 2026 urgency trigger for coding-agent governance
findings.statement: The Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force 27 July 2026) moved stand-alone Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 Dec 2027 and Annex I to 2 Aug 2028; Article 50 transparency applied from 2 Aug 2026; GPAI obligations from 2 Aug 2025; AI literacy from 2 Feb 2025. Internal software-development agents are generally not Annex III systems, so EU compliance pressure on engineering teams is indirect (via products they build for high-risk uses). ISO/IEC 42001 functions as a vendor trust signal (Anthropic certified Jan 2025).
findings.limitations: Official Journal text not fetched directly; legal applicability to a given client requires counsel. Not legal advice.

findings.title: Echelon's flagship differentiator is implemented but not in use
findings.statement: Praxis main (3.25.0, 2026-11-03) states 'Mandatory verified completion is not enabled across Echelon repositories'; attested completion requires a pinned verifier key (owner decision OD-9 open). As of 2026-10-23 the end-to-end integration intake->Ordo->Dokimos->Praxis was status 5 (not specified/connected) and 287 of 307 execution records carried no tokens. The released approved set 1.26.0 could not attest completion (no Dokimos 0.7.0 in catalog). Verified completion, provenance and cost telemetry therefore cannot honestly be sold as a licensed, production-proven product today.
findings.limitations: Status of later releases (Dokimos 0.11.1, Praxis 3.25.0) beyond the rollout doc was not re-inventoried by G; Track C/E may update.

findings.title: Echelon's own experiments show cost overhead without a measured quality gain on current fixtures
findings.statement: REL-001 run-02: every arm 39/39 correct; optimized Echelon cost $0.1555 vs bare agent $0.1147 per correct requirement (+35.5%). Executable authorization was harmful (VAC-002-P3), typed records did not reduce errors. Positive, commercially usable results are method insights: brief-level architecture guidance removed violations (ARCH-002, Supported) and agent continuity cut cost per accepted requirement ~40% (VAC-001). These transfer best as consulting know-how, not as a licensed control product.
findings.limitations: Ceiling effects on fixtures; one model family; quality benefit on harder, real work is untested (Track D).

findings.title: Independent, attested 'definition of done' separated from the agent vendor appears unoccupied
findings.statement: Vendor materials reviewed describe agent self-review (Copilot coding agent), AI code review (CodeRabbit, Qodo), quality gates (Sonar), evaluations (AgentCore, Foundry) and audit logs, but none of the reviewed pages describes a verifier independent of the implementing agent that signs a completion receipt bound to requirement IDs and revision. Echelon's REL-001 C3b/GATE-3 showed self-produced evidence can be forged, which is the argument for independence. This is the most distinctive position available, if it holds up.
findings.limitations: Absence of evidence on marketing pages is weak; supply-chain attestation tooling (SLSA/in-toto, artifact attestations) not surveyed; buyers may not value independence enough to pay.

findings.title: Public Echelon site makes outcome claims without located evidence
findings.statement: echelon-foundry site source claims '40%+ throughput gains' and 'reconciliation times reduced 80%'. No evidence packet for these claims was located in the repositories reviewed. For a brand built on evidence and on 'overclaiming is the most frequent recurring failure' (internal consolidation), unsupported headline numbers are a commercial and credibility risk.
findings.limitations: Evidence may exist privately (e.g. research-documents or client files) — not searched exhaustively; truth of claims NOT TESTED.

findings.title: Managed software factory / outcome-based delivery is not ready
findings.statement: The hypothesis that Echelon can sell outcome-based delivery now is contradicted by its own record: Rehearsal 1 passed but with 25 defects; Rehearsal 2's self-declared acceptance is INVALID under the ledger contract (721 min vs 420-min ceiling); Rehearsal 3 NOT ACCEPTED. Market direction does favour outcome pricing (Deloitte DART accounting guidance June 2026; Deloitte predictions), and model cost is small ($0.11-$0.16 per correct requirement on fixtures), so the binding constraint is delivery predictability and acceptance, not compute.
findings.limitations: Rehearsal tasks are one application family; future rehearsals may change this.

findings.title: Coding-agent usage is concentrating on a few platforms that Echelon depends on
findings.statement: Among Stack Overflow 2026 coding-agent users, Claude Code (66%) and GitHub Copilot (59%) lead; Cognition reported a $492M run-rate (May 2026). Echelon should position as an agent-agnostic evidence layer over Claude Code/Copilot/Codex rather than as another agent, and track platform risk if Anthropic or GitHub add independent completion verification.
findings.limitations: SO 2026 published as editorial highlights; full dataset pending; revenue figures company-reported.

findings.title: Large AI services spend exists, but its size says nothing about Echelon's addressable market
findings.statement: Gartner (Sept 2026) forecasts 2026 AI services spending around $576.5B and AI software around $461.6B within ~$2.67T total AI spending. These figures confirm a large consulting/services budget category but are proprietary forecasts with broad category boundaries; no serviceable-market estimate for Echelon is derived or claimed.
findings.limitations: Figures via search summary of the release table; methodology proprietary; quoted for context only.
